Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has replied to XRP holders who criticized him for selling most of his XRP with a Saturday Night Live GIF of Natalie Portman saying, "I never said I was a role model."

According to Schwartz, his XRP holdings are down 88%, from a peak of roughly 26 million tokens to 3 million. His Bitcoin went from about 1,500 coins to one, and his Ether went from about 40,000 to six.

Schwartz wrote that he "really doesn't like risk." According to Schwartz, he and his wife agreed years ago to sell some of their coins every time crypto reached a new all-time high. In 2025, Schwartz sold around 2.5 million XRP and paid about $1.7 million in capital gains tax on the sale. He had received these tokens in 2020 and 2023.

@hllywd22 @tchdwntommyd @WHTBOYRICKY @CryptoTaxFixer When XRP hit 10 cents, that seemed ridiculous. When ETH hit $1, that seemed ridiculous. What BTC hit $200, that seemed ridiculous.

Schwartz said that all of his sales were made under written trading plans, and a lawyer approved each plan at least 30 days before each sale. According to Schwartz, his largest risk asset is still his stake in Ripple.

Schwartz also said that he was a skeptic from the start and did not believe in the early price records of crypto. "When XRP hit 10 cents, that seemed ridiculous. When ETH hit $1, that seemed ridiculous," he wrote.

In his view, the price of XRP today depends on overall sentiment in the crypto market, and fees on the network barely move it. Schwartz allows that the token could capture some of the value of a successful ecosystem in the future, but there are no guarantees. On Monday, the price of XRP stands at $0.956.

On Nov. 16, Schwartz also posted a review of the XRPL codebase by the Qwen AI model. "I asked Qwen to rate my work on the XRPL software. It was mostly good. But this was harsh and it's not wrong," he wrote.

According to the review, the overall architecture of XRPL is good. Still, Qwen said that some components of the code are too tightly coupled, and the migration to a new testing framework stopped halfway. The AI model also called the code generation in XRPL opaque.

Several XRPL developers replied to the post and said that they are already rewriting some of these parts of the code. Other users asked for formal verification of the XRPL core before the new features planned for 2027 go live.

#5138. Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

Bitcoin news: BTC hit $67,568 as longs were liquidated. Fear is Extreme, but BTC fell further after 15 of 16 past readings.

In Bitcoin news on Friday, November 13, the BTC USD price fell as low as $67,568 on Binance as a wave of forced selling wiped out leveraged bets on a rebound. It was the cryptocurrency’s lowest price since August 19.

Bitcoin trades at $68,772, down 6.7% in 24 hours and 9.1% in a week. Ether lost 5.5% and Solana 3.4% on the day.

BREAKING: Bitcoin falls below $69,000 and ETH nears $1,900 as selling pressure accelerates in crypto.

Crypto markets have now lost -$150 billion in 48 hours. pic.twitter.com/29QW0khxOh

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 13, 2026

Most of the damage came from liquidations, when an exchange closes a leveraged trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out. CoinGlass data cited by several outlets put the 24-hour total at about $1.4 billion, close to 90% of it from longs, the bets that prices would rise. Those forced sales pushed Bitcoin through $70,000 in about two hours overnight.

The mood has flipped with it. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index dropped from 28 to 20 on Friday, its first Extreme Fear reading since July.

In Bitcoin news this week, the question is no longer whether the market is scared. It is whether Extreme Fear means the bottom is close, and what the daily and weekly charts say.

The slide started on Thursday afternoon, when Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. It picked up speed after midnight UTC, when Bitcoin broke below the $72,727 low from Tuesday and kept falling.

We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours.

Investors have also kept pulling money from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, funds that buy and hold the coin itself, adding to the selling.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

On Thursday, we listed three signs that would point to a bottom: the fear index dropping toward the teens, the funding rate turning negative and open interest, the value of open futures bets, falling as longs give up. Overnight, two of them showed up.

One sign still points the other way. On OKX, 3.19 accounts are long for every one that is short, about the same as before the crash. Many traders are still buying the dip with leverage.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Extreme Fear sounds like a buy signal. History says it usually comes early. We found every time since 2018 that the index first dropped to 20 or lower after at least a month without such a reading. There were 16, and we followed Bitcoin for 90 days after each.

The most recent case fits the pattern. Extreme Fear first appeared on June 3 at $64,014, and Bitcoin still fell another 8.5% before it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1. Then it rallied to $87,396 in September.

For anyone reading this Bitcoin news as a buy signal, Extreme Fear says the bottom is getting closer. It has rarely said the bottom is here. A move to the 2026 lows would match the median path.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, Bitcoin sits far below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA is at $78,226 and the 200-day EMA at $76,325.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, the key level is the 200-week EMA at $69,555. Bitcoin trades just below it, and the week closes on Sunday.

That line matters. Bitcoin closed below the 200-week EMA for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of 2026’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

The overnight flush did part of the work a bottom needs: leverage came out and funding turned negative.

For traders following Bitcoin news, the Sunday weekly close against $69,555 is the next test. History says the final low often comes weeks after the first Extreme Fear reading.

#5135. Satoshi’s Bitcoin DNA in XRP Ledger Uncovered in Two Cryptographic Mechanisms

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. XRP Ledger Foundation Director of Community Hussein Zangana (Vet) shared a tidbit of XRPL's early history in a recent X post.

Vet noted that the XRP Ledger (XRPL) still carries traces of Satoshi Nakamoto’s original Bitcoin design, highlighting two features.

In 2011, three engineers—David Schwartz, Jed McCaleb, and Arthur Britto—began developing the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Fascinated by Bitcoin, they set out to create a better version that improved upon its limitations—with the goal of creating a digital asset that was more sustainable and built specifically for payments.

As reported, the first line of code for the core of what would become the XRP Ledger (XRPL) was written by David Schwartz, who is Ripple CTO emeritus, about 15 years ago, on November 11, 2011.

Vet delves into the earliest part of XRP Ledger history, noting that 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, wrote. Vet added that Jed McCaleb also copied Satoshi’s timekeeping code into the XRPL, even including one of the Bitcoin creator’s comments shared as a screenshot.

Did you know all of us on the XRP Ledger use design choices by Satoshi daily? 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Satoshi wrote. Jed copied Satoshi's timekeeping code into the XRPL, including one of Satoshi's comments. By the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone. In December 2014, Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment. Two design choices of Satoshi still remain on the XRPL and all of us use at least one of it. Signature curve secp256k1 (we also support Ed25519 thus not everyone uses this) and how XRPL addresses are generated from the public key with SHA-256 followed by RIPEMD-160, that's what all of us use.

The quote "Never go to sea with two chronometers; take one or three" is a classic maritime adage famously included by Satoshi Nakamoto (the pseudonymous creator of Bitcoin) within the Bitcoin source code.

Vet explained that by the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone from the XRP Ledger. In December 2014, former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment.

However, two of Satoshi's design choices still remain on the XRP Ledger: the first is the secp256k1 signature curve, which Bitcoin uses and which the XRP Ledger continues to support. However, the ledger also supports Ed25519, meaning not every XRPL user relies on secp256k1.

"I remember David saying they used secp256k1 so no one would doubt the security because it's the same as Bitcoin's, etc.," Vet stated, citing the insight of the Ripple CTO emeritus on secp256k1, adding, "Lots of interesting things to dig into from the early days."

The second is the method used to generate XRP Ledger addresses from public keys. The process applies SHA-256 hashing followed by RIPEMD-160, a design inherited from Bitcoin that remains common to all XRPL addresses.

Asked why the timekeeping code and Satoshi's comment were removed, Vet explained that this became leftover code as new code was introduced, so it was cleaned up.

Cardano DReps have rejected a proposal by Toto Finance to spend 22 million ADA from the Cardano treasury on a "Strategic Copper Reserve."

The vote closed on Nov. 15, and DReps holding 2.86 billion ADA voted against the proposal, according to Cardano governance data. DReps with 20.02 million ADA voted in favor of it.

DRep John MacPherson was among those who voted "No," and he explained his decision in a post on X.

MacPherson wrote that he is not against real-world assets on Cardano. Still, he said the proposal asks the treasury "to take on both the copper price and the ada price," and Toto Finance would collect "up to about 3.4M ada in fees."

At the same time, MacPherson said that the proposal is “more honest about its risks than most.”

Toto Finance, a company led by Monty Metzger, submitted the proposal on Oct. 15. ADA is trading at $0.152 on Monday, and the requested 22 million ADA is now worth around $3.3 million.

The plan was to buy copper with 14.72 million ADA and store it in a warehouse near New Orleans. Toto Finance wanted to issue one CuTT token for each pound of copper. The metal would be sold in 18 to 24 months.

The Cardano Foundation, which votes as a DRep, announced its "No" vote in October.

"We recognize the opportunity in real-world asset tokenization; however, this proposal places 22,000,000 ada under the recipient's sole control to fund a fee-heavy concentrated commodity position whose safeguards are not yet in place," the foundation wrote.

Three members of the Constitutional Committee voted "No," and the other four members did not vote.

Crypto commentator Ingeniero Cripto agreed with MacPherson in the replies under his post. He called the "double exposure" to the prices of copper and ADA the key problem of the proposal, as the Cardano treasury already holds ADA.

According to him, RWAs on Cardano make sense, but “funding the asset itself is a different question than funding the rails.”

#5132. Bitcoin Demand Dries Up as Miners Prepare to Dump 2,077 BTC: Is More Selling Pressure Coming for BTC?

Bitcoin demand weakens as miners transfer 2,077 BTC to exchanges; Antpool accounting for 97% ahead of an estimated 8% mining difficulty cut.

Bitcoin (BTC) demand is showing signs of weakness as miners move more coins to cryptocurrency exchanges. CryptoQuant recorded 2,077 BTC in miner-to-exchange transfers on November 10, approximately 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. The move comes as Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum and the network approaches an estimated 8% reduction in mining difficulty.

The latest figures raise concerns about potential selling pressure, particularly as demand indicators weaken across spot and derivatives markets.

Meanwhile, miners could soon receive some relief from lower network difficulty.

Bitcoin's Rebound Fades as Spot Demand Weakens and Miner Flows Surge

“Leverage is being unwound, but spot demand has not recovered sustainably.” – By @xwinfinance pic.twitter.com/n03axjQKqt

— CryptoQuant.com (@cryptoquant_com) November 13, 2026

Explore: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

The 2,077 BTC transfer marked the largest daily miner-to-exchange movement since February 2026, according to CryptoQuant. Around 97% of the transferred Bitcoin came from Antpool, one of the network’s largest mining pools.

The movement represents a significant increase compared with the 30-day average of 127 BTC. Miners often transfer Bitcoin to exchanges when they need to liquidate holdings to cover electricity bills, equipment costs and other operating expenses.

However, CryptoQuant’s Miner to Exchange Flow indicator tracks transfers rather than completed sales. Miners can also move coins for treasury management or other operational reasons.

The latest activity therefore signals a potential increase in available selling supply, rather than confirmation that 2,077 BTC entered the market as sell orders.

Miner transfers are adding to concerns about an already fragile market. CryptoQuant’s 30-day demand-growth indicators showed negative readings across both spot and perpetual futures markets.

Spot demand stood at approximately -280,000 BTC, while perpetual futures demand reached around -82,000 BTC. Combined, the indicators produced a negative reading of approximately 362,000 BTC.

These figures point to deteriorating demand conditions. Spot demand is particularly important because it reflects activity in the underlying Bitcoin market, while perpetual futures activity provides insight into speculative positioning.

The negative readings suggest that buying activity has struggled to absorb available supply. If miners continue transferring Bitcoin to exchanges while spot demand remains weak, the market could face additional downward pressure.

However, these indicators measure changes in estimated demand, not a direct count of Bitcoin sold by investors.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Bitcoin’s next difficulty adjustment, expected around 14 November at block 975,744, may drop by roughly 8.4% after average block times rose to 655 seconds. The protocol reduces difficulty every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks) to maintain a 10-minute target; slower production eases mining and may boost BTC yield per unit of power.

This could aid miners amid weak prices and tight margins, but profitability still depends on electricity costs, hardware efficiency, fees and BTC value.

Bitcoin is trading near $69,200 after another sharp daily decline. The chart shows that BTC has broken below the $75,000–$76,000 support zone, which now represents an important resistance area. The immediate level to watch is around $69,000.

A sustained break below it could expose the $64,000–$65,000 support area, followed by $60,000. On the upside, Bitcoin would need to reclaim $75,000 to signal a potential recovery and improve its short-term outlook.

Bitcoin faces several challenges heading into the next difficulty adjustment. The increase in miner-to-exchange transfers, combined with negative demand indicators, suggests that the market is struggling to attract sufficient buying interest.

Still, the Antpool transfers should not be interpreted as proof of widespread miner capitulation. The data identifies a large movement from one mining pool, but does not establish that the coins were sold.

The upcoming difficulty reduction could improve mining conditions and help struggling operators manage their costs. However, it is unlikely to resolve the broader weakness in Bitcoin demand.

Investors will be watching whether exchange transfers translate into actual selling and whether spot-market buyers return. A recovery in demand would help absorb additional supply and provide a stronger foundation for Bitcoin’s next move.

#5130. After 7 Years and 99% Speed Leap, Solana (SOL) Finally Drops Its 'Beta' Label

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Solana has officially removed the "beta" tag from its mainnet's name and introduced the Solana 1.0 standard. The switch was announced on Nov. 16 at the Breakpoint conference in London.

"Solana 1.0 marks the network's graduation from 'mainnet beta' to 'mainnet,' retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch," the Solana Foundation said.

Solana launched on March 16, 2020, and the network had been working under the "mainnet-beta" label for six years and eight months. According to the foundation, the label "never evolved to signal its production status."

The Solana Foundation coordinated the rollout with the Anza and Firedancer teams. Co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko replied to the announcement on X with three exploding-head emojis.

"For users, this is the same network, nothing changes. Your SOL, accounts, assets, applications, and transaction history remain the same," the foundation wrote. On Monday, SOL is trading at $71.35.

According to the foundation, two upgrades made the change possible. In October, Solana activated Alpenglow with the Agave 4.3 release, and the time to final confirmation went down by almost 99%, from 12.8 seconds to around 150 milliseconds.

Firedancer, a validator client developed by Jump Crypto independently from Agave, is also now running on the Solana mainnet. Independent implementations "limit the impact of bugs affecting one client, and strengthen network resilience," the foundation said.

Solana 1.0 also gives the network a shared protocol version, and it does not depend on the version numbers of individual clients such as Agave and Firedancer.

"A shared protocol version lets everyone refer to Solana's evolution without using one client's release number as shorthand for the entire network," the Solana Foundation explained. "Announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement at once."

Earlier this year, Solana raised the compute limit per block from 60 million to 100 million compute units in May, and the slot time went down from 400 to 200 milliseconds in August. The maximum transaction size also went up from 1,232 to 4,096 bytes.

"Documentation, websites, explorers, and other ecosystem surfaces will progressively reflect the updated designation," the foundation added.

Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, spent $228.1 million buying back its STRC preferred stock between Nov. 9 and Nov. 15, according to the company's new filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Over the same period, Strategy bought 485 BTC for $33.4 million, so the company spent almost seven times more on STRC than on Bitcoin.

"Strategy has acquired 485 BTC and repurchased $228M of STRC. As of 11/15/26, we hold 850,849 BTC and $4.9B of USD Assets," Michael Saylor wrote on X.

The filing shows that Strategy sold 2.09 million shares of its Class A common stock and raised $244.7 million. The company used $206.3 million of that amount for STRC buybacks and added another $21.8 million from interest earned on its dollar reserves.

The 485 BTC were bought at an average price of $68,887 per coin. The remaining $5 million from the share sales stayed on the books as free cash.

STRC, also known as Stretch, is a perpetual preferred stock with a variable monthly dividend, and Strategy launched it in July 2025.

When the price of Bitcoin slipped below $65,000, STRC fell to $99.08. Strategy aims to keep STRC close to its $100 par value, and the company has another $332.2 million set aside for buybacks. The board of Strategy also approved a December STRC dividend at an annual rate of 12%, or $1.00 per share.

"USD Duration is 3.4 yrs and STRC's BTC Credit tightened to 67 bps (-3 bps), assuming 10% BTC ARR, 40% BTC Vol, and a BTC price of $68,800," Saylor added.

As of Nov. 15, Strategy held 850,849 BTC, bought for a total of $64.2 billion at an average price of $75,452 per coin. On Monday, the price of Bitcoin stands at $63,941, and Strategy's holdings are worth around $54.4 billion.

The unrealized loss of the company on its Bitcoin holdings stands at around $9.8 billion. On Sunday, when the price of Bitcoin fell to $62,029 on Bitfinex, the loss was above $11 billion.

Strategy also holds $4.9 billion in dollar assets, and $4.75 billion of that amount is in its dedicated USD reserve.

Apple said Tuesday’s disruption to iCloud, the App Store and Apple Pay stemmed from an internal update, while Chase blamed a software bug in on-premise systems for Monday’s banking failure. CNN and Reuters reported no immediate evidence of a cyberattack behind the collapse of the NSA’s classified internal network the same day. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said CISA had seen no traffic pointing to an attack, though he separately floated superintelligence as a possible cause, telling Fox News, “I believe that it’s the SI.” The FBI issued a FLASH advisory on Tuesday warning that hackers are using an AI-driven tool called ARTEX to automate intrusions, but the bureau has not linked it to any of the outages.

#5122. US and Canada Announce Massive Crypto Fraud Crackdown

Authorities in the United States and Canada have announced a major cross-border crackdown on cryptocurrency fraud, bringing together law enforcement agencies, financial regulators and private companies to target online scam networks.

The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) announced on Nov. 16 the launch of Operation Niagara, a coordinated initiative aimed at disrupting organized cryptocurrency fraud schemes and protecting potential victims.

According to the Canadian securities regulator, the operation involves investigators, securities specialists and financial crime experts from both countries.

The initiative will use advanced technology and enhanced investigative capabilities to identify fraudulent activity and potential victims in near real time.

Importantly, the operation will not focus solely on investigating criminals after fraud has occurred. Authorities also intend to identify individuals who are being targeted by scammers and intervene before they suffer further financial losses.

"Fraud knows no border, and it targets everyday people," said Bonnie Lysyk, Executive Vice-President of Enforcement at the OSC.

The initiative brings together several major law enforcement and regulatory agencies, including the U.S. Secret Service, Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) and Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP).

Canadian securities regulators, including the Alberta Securities Commission, British Columbia Securities Commission and Autorité des marchés financiers, are also participating.

Private-sector companies will contribute technical expertise and intelligence to help authorities identify and disrupt fraudulent networks.

It’s worth noting that the OSC didn’t provide details on how many fraud networks it is targeting, how many potential victims have been identified or how much cryptocurrency is involved in Operation Niagara.

If ETH follows same path as SPCX IPO, $ETH bottoms shortly before $ANT IPO https://t.co/FS6T3KiRpo

SpaceX raised a record $75 billion in its IPO in June. The bottom for ETH came three trading days before SpaceX priced its shares, and the price of ETH went up after that.

BitMine now holds 6,077,745 ETH, or 4.97% of all coins in circulation (about 122.2 million ETH), and it is the world's largest corporate Ethereum treasury. According to the company, it is 99% of the way through its "Alchemy of 5%" program, and fewer than 35,000 ETH are left to reach the target.

The total portfolio of BitMine, which includes crypto, cash, securities and venture stakes, has shrunk from a peak of more than $14 billion to $11.8 billion. According to BitMine, 5,227,037 ETH, or around 86% of the reserve, is staked.

Lee expects the growth cycle for ETH to last two to three years, driven by bank tokenization, and his base-case targets for ETH range from $12,000 to $22,000.

Bitcoin fell 19% into the biggest IPO ever. Now it's down 18% heading into the second biggest.

SpaceX raised $75B when it went public on June 12. In the 50 days before it listed, Bitcoin dropped 19%. Anthropic plans to raise up to $64B when it lists next week, and Bitcoin is… pic.twitter.com/pRAkGpxr1z

— Matt Cole (@ColeMacro) November 13, 2026

Some traders think giant IPOs pull money out of crypto as investors sell other assets to buy in. Here is what Bitcoin did before, during and after the SpaceX listing, and what that could mean for the Anthropic debut.

SpaceX made its filing public on May 20 and set a fixed price of $135 a share on June 1. Nasdaq listed its Class A shares on June 12.

The recovery came later. By September 10, 90 days after the listing, Bitcoin was back near where it started, and it reached $87,396 on September 21.

For this Bitcoin news analysis, we indexed Bitcoin’s daily closes to 24 days before each listing: May 19 for SpaceX and October 26 for Anthropic. The two lines start and end in almost the same place.

If Bitcoin follows the SpaceX script, the listing itself would bring a short relief bounce, not the bottom.

Two IPOs are not a pattern, and the timing in this Bitcoin news may be a coincidence. Both slides also had other causes, such as forced selling of leveraged bets. Still, the June playbook says the listing day is a poor guide to the bottom.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, Bitcoin trades at $64,560. It sits far below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $76,680, and its 200-day EMA at $75,977.

#5110. Nvidia and IBM’s 13,000x Quantum Speedup Raises New ‘Q-Day’ Questions for Bitcoin

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Nvidia, IBM and Fermilab announced new tools for quantum error correction on Nov. 16, and the news comes amid a debate in the crypto industry about "Q-Day," the moment when a quantum computer will be able to break Bitcoin's cryptography. As of Monday, the price of Bitcoin stands at $64,580.

Nvidia released a new decoding algorithm, TCBP-JOBS, on Nov. 16. According to the company, the algorithm delivers up to 13,000x faster decoding compared with existing leading algorithms, and it cuts the computation time for researching new quantum computing designs from 12 weeks to 45 minutes.

Nvidia said that the algorithm helps researchers find designs that use physical qubits more efficiently, "shortening the path to practical fault-tolerant quantum computing."

Nvidia and IBM also announced plans for a modular quantum computing codesign platform with Fermilab. IBM and Nvidia are placing Nvidia DGX B200 systems next to IBM quantum computers, including those powered by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, and researchers will use the platform to develop and test error-correction codes.

"Making quantum computers useful for science requires advances in error correction, applications and the systems that bring quantum processors and accelerated computing together," said Krysta Svore, vice president of applied research for quantum computing at Nvidia.

A 2022 study by researchers from the University of Sussex estimated that breaking Bitcoin's encryption within a day would require around 13 million physical qubits.

IBM Quantum Nighthawk, which IBM calls its fastest quantum processor, has 120 qubits. According to Nvidia, errors in quantum processors "limit the complexity and duration of the computations they can perform."

In 2024, Bitcoin developer Hunter Beast proposed BIP-360, a new output type that would protect coins from quantum attacks. In July 2025, Casa co-founder Jameson Lopp also suggested a plan to phase out legacy signatures and move coins to quantum-resistant addresses.

Early coins mined by Satoshi Nakamoto sit on addresses with public keys that are already visible on the blockchain.

In November 2024, NIST proposed to stop allowing vulnerable public-key algorithms, including elliptic curve cryptography, after 2035.

#5106. Harvard Refuses to Dump Bitcoin Holdings Despite Downturn

Elite university Harvard maintains significant Bitcoin exposure as it holds over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin ETF, a recent regulatory filing has revealed.

Harvard University remains highly exposed to Bitcoin (BTC) as the elite institution continues to hold over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF).

As per Bitcoin Magazine’s Nov. 16 report, Harvard Management Company, which manages Harvard University’s endowment, held 3,044,612 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

The Form 13F filing by Harvard University with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) showed that its investment in the Bitcoin ETF was worth roughly $144.1 million at the end of the third quarter.

Notably, Harvard did not change its Bitcoin ETF share count during the third quarter. The university held the same number of shares as reported at the end of June.

Harvard first disclosed its investment in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF during the second quarter of 2025.

As per Harvard's Form 13F filing submitted on Aug. 8, 2025, it held 1,906,000 IBIT shares at the end of the second quarter. The investment was worth roughly $116.7 million as of June 30.

The university subsequently increased its Bitcoin exposure significantly.

For instance, at the end of September 2025, Harvard held 6,813,612 IBIT shares, worth roughly $442.9 million. The Bitcoin ETF was the biggest investment that Harvard publicly reported at the time.

Later, however, the university started trimming its Bitcoin exposure. For example, during the fourth quarter of 2025, Harvard reduced its IBIT holdings by about 21.4%. Its total share holdings fell to 5.35 million.

During the first quarter of 2026, Harvard again reduced its Bitcoin exposure by 43.1%. This brought down the number of IBIT shares to roughly 3.04 million.

Since then, the university has maintained this number of shares. Harvard's quarter-end share count has remained unchanged in recent quarters.

Harvard University is not the only top-tier American university that has gained exposure to the biggest cryptocurrency by market capitalization.

In October 2024, Emory University became the first U.S. university endowment to publicly disclose its holdings in a Bitcoin ETF.

It held roughly 2.7 million shares of Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust, worth over $15 million at the time.

Meanwhile, in May 2025, Brown University disclosed its holdings of 105,000 shares of BlackRock's IBIT, worth roughly $4.9 million as of March 31 of that year.

Later, Brown doubled its stake, bringing its holdings to 212,500 shares.

Meanwhile, Dartmouth College has also joined the list of universities with exposure to cryptocurrency ETFs.

In its recent filing, Dartmouth College disclosed that it held 201,531 IBIT shares. The investment was worth roughly $9.5 million as of the end of September 2026.

#5102. Ripple's Schwartz Reveals Why XRP Ledger Used Satoshi's Code

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has shared the reason the XRP Ledger (XRPL) used code and cryptography from Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, in its early stages.

In his Nov. 16 post on X, Schwartz said they primarily chose to do so for security reasons and to prevent backlash from the Bitcoin community when the XRP Ledger was still in its early development.

The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.

Vet said that the XRP Ledger initially used helper functions from the original Bitcoin software, including timekeeping functions coded by Satoshi Nakamoto himself.

Some of those helper functions were reportedly copied by Jed McCaleb, one of the early developers of the XRP Ledger. The original Bitcoin code even included a comment left by the mysterious creator of Bitcoin.

Afterward, Schwartz shared the reason why XRP Ledger developers opted to use the cryptographic options from Bitcoin instead of creating new ones.

"We did things that way in the very early days because we didn't want to be potentially facing criticism that our choices for those core crypto functions were less secure than Bitcoin's," said Schwartz.

In other words, XRP Ledger developers opted to use Bitcoin's cryptographic options to avoid possible controversial security-related decisions when creating a new cryptocurrency network.

Later on, Vet asked Schwartz if their decision helped gain acceptance among Bitcoin supporters who looked at their protocol in its early stages.

Schwartz said it was hard to say whether it helped or not.

"It's hard to say. Obviously we never got those criticisms. But it's hard to know if we would have," Schwartz said.

Additionally, the Ripple executive pointed out that it was uncertain whether the developers could have come up with better options if they had chosen to make their own cryptographic decisions.

"I'm not sure we would have come up with better ones had we made our own decisions anyway," Schwartz wrote.

It is worth noting that the original Bitcoin code copied in the early stages of the XRP Ledger is no longer present in the network's codebase.

According to Vet, the remaining parts of Satoshi Nakamoto's timekeeping code were deleted in December 2014 by former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis.

There are two crucial cryptographic design decisions from Bitcoin that are still used on the XRP Ledger.

#5095. Hong Kong’s SWIFT Push Puts XRP Back In Focus

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Hong Kong’s SWIFT Push Puts XRP Back In Focus

Programmable blockchain payments are coming: Swift is plugging its ledger into Hong Kong’s Project Ensemble.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced on 16 November, 2026 a strengthened partnership with Swift to explore how tokenised deposits can improve the speed and end-to-end experience of cross-border transactions.

The work builds on collaboration that began in 2023 through the Project Ensemble Sandbox, where the two organisations tested interoperability between central bank digital currency systems.

The latest phase brings in major Hong Kong banks, including Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered, and HSBC, to examine how the Swift ledger can connect with Project Ensemble’s settlement layer.

The goal is to develop mechanisms that use multi-currency tokenised deposits for cross-border payments, using Swift’s global network to link international and local systems more tightly.

HKMA Deputy Chief Executive Howard Lee described it as another step toward supporting real-time, always-on, and programmable cross-border transactions.

Swift is plugging its ledger into Hong Kong's Project Ensemble.The HKMA, Swift, HSBC, Standard Chartered and Bank of China (Hong Kong) will explore moving tokenized deposits across borders in multiple currencies. The goal is real-time, 24/7, programmable payments.It's still…

Swift’s Chief Business Officer Thierry Chilosi noted that as domestic systems evolve to handle new forms of digital value, the organisation is exploring how its ledger can connect these platforms across borders so institutions can settle more efficiently.

This is not Hong Kong’s first experiment with tokenised assets and digital money infrastructure. In 2023, Ripple and Fubon Bank participated in the HKMA’s inaugural e-HKD Pilot Programme.

Their use case combined a hypothetical e-HKD with tokenised real estate (property liens) and lending protocols to enable faster access to home equity.

The solution ran on a private ledger built with the same technology as the XRP Ledger, with Ripple’s CBDC platform handling the digital currency layer.

That earlier pilot focused on domestic retail and asset-tokenisation scenarios. The new HKMA x Swift x XRP work shifts the emphasis toward wholesale interbank settlement and multi-currency cross-border flows using tokenised deposits.

Both efforts share the same underlying requirement: different systems, whether CBDC platforms, tokenized deposit ledgers, or traditional messaging networks, must be able to interoperate without forcing every participant on one rail.

Public blockchains such as the XRP Ledger have long been positioned by their proponents as neutral settlement layers that can sit between otherwise incompatible systems.

HKMA + SWIFT + tokenized deposits is a peak "TradFi meets onchain" moment 🤝 honest q fam: would you hold tokenized bank deposits, or stick with stablecoins? 🤔

XRP itself is frequently discussed as a potential bridge asset for currency conversions in corridors where no single national digital currency is suitable as an intermediary.

Ripple’s earlier work with the HKMA already demonstrated that XRPL-derived technology could support tokenized asset and CBDC-related use cases inside a regulated pilot.

The current Project Ensemble-Swift collaboration does not name any public blockchain or bridge asset. The programme focuses on connecting existing institutional infrastructure with emerging tokenised-deposit systems.

Some reasons for rejection were the concerns raised about fees. Representatives noted that only two-thirds of the fees would be used to actually buy the copper. Moreover, there was no clear custody protection in place, with some representatives opposing a venture into a private commodity.

However, some users argue that a copper supplier could back the tokens with metal it already owns. Thus, Cardano could test demand for tokenized copper without putting the ADA treasury on the hook for storage fees and swings in the metal prices.

But the move was more of a win for Cardano holders as they protected their treasury.

36 hours. 179 hackers. 70 submissions. At the XRP Ledger Hackathon, developers used Mastercard Agent Pay for machines to explore new possibilities for micropayments and autonomous commerce, including how AI agents can transact within defined spending limits and with verified merchants. See what we learned about the future of agentic commerce: https://t.co/S4NwQxxuRi #AgenticCommerce #DigitalAssets #AI

Global payments giant Mastercard recently posted on X about the outcome of the XRP Ledger Hackathon. In the post, the payments firm detailed that 179 developers submitted 70 projects during the 36-hour event in Manhattan.

The focus of the competition was how to enable AI-powered agents to autonomously execute transactions and micropayments, engage with verified merchants and so forth, all while operating within budgets set by developers.

The hackathon was held as part of the preparations for Ripple’s annual conference called Swell. Mastercard, Amazon Web Services, QuickNode and Ledger supported the event, which had a prize pool of over $40,000.

#5092. 178 Websites Infected in Major Optimizely Hack: Crypto Wallets Targeted, but Bitcoin Barely Reacted

Optimizely attack infects 178 websites, steals crypto and card data, and exposes users to wallet-address swaps and iPhone exploits.

An Optimizely attack on Monday, November 16, planted crypto-stealing code on the websites of 178 organizations, including Ledger, HSBC, Zoom, the BBC and CNN. The malicious script swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed card numbers, and tried to break into iPhones for about 19 hours before it was cleaned up.

BREAKING: A cyberattack hit 178 major organizations, including Zoom, CNN, BBC, Fox News, HSBC, Ledger, Equifax, Salesforce, IKEA and Air France-KLM, by loading malware on the Optimizely Web platform, exposing visitors to scripts built to steal payment data and exploit iOS…

— The Hormuz Letter (@HormuzLetter) November 17, 2026

Optimizely is a tool companies use to test different versions of their web pages. An attacker slipped code into the scripts it serves, so every site that loaded them ran the malware.

We traced the attacker’s Bitcoin wallet. It received five payments worth about $5,500, and one victim alone sent nearly 90% of it. Bitcoin barely moved while the attack ran.

So what happened, and what is the real impact of hacks like this one?

Security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI found the code and published a full breakdown. The attacker wrote it into a settings field in customers’ Optimizely projects, so it was served from Optimizely’s own servers and looked legitimate.

Optimizely said it “secured affected user accounts and added protections against further unauthorized code delivery.” Report URI found no sign that Ledger hardware wallets themselves were breached. The danger was on the website, where a copied address could be swapped before a user pasted it.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

Report URI listed the attacker’s wallets. We checked the Bitcoin one on mempool.space, the public Bitcoin block explorer.

The Optimizely attack’s impact was tiny, and the market ignored it. Bitcoin is near $64,300 after its weekend low of $62,006, and that slide came from wider selling, not this attack.

EXPLORE: Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 Billion in 2026, More Than Triple 2025: How Did Bitcoin and Ether React?

The money stolen in the Optimizely attack is small, but the method is the year’s most damaging one. We sorted DefiLlama’s 2026 hack list by attack type. Attacks on websites and infrastructure, rather than on smart contracts, are now the costliest category:

These attacks hit users where no wallet setting can protect them. The fix is on the user’s side: check the address on the hardware wallet’s screen before signing, send a small test transfer first, and keep phones updated.

On the daily chart, Bitcoin trades at $64,326. It sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $76,208, and its 200-day EMA at $75,864.

The Optimizely attack did not move Bitcoin, and the attacker walked away with about $7,000. Its real cost is trust: when a hardware-wallet maker’s own website can serve malware for hours, checking every address on the device is no longer optional.

#5089. CFTC Makes Historic Move With Blockchain Derivatives Approval

The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened historic doors for blockchain technology adoption in traditional financial markets as it approves exchange and clearinghouse applications for blockchain-based derivatives market infrastructure.

On Nov. 16, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig announced that the commission had given the green light to exchange (designated contract market or DCM) and clearinghouse (derivatives clearing organization or DCO) applications for a company using blockchain technology for the execution and settlement of derivatives contracts.

As per the official statement, Selig considers this a major step forward for U.S. financial markets. He said that blockchain-based market infrastructure is compatible with current U.S. financial regulations.

"This approval makes clear that there is a regulatory path for companies that want to innovate and use blockchain technology to modernize how derivatives are traded and settled,"  he elaborated.

Selig pointed out that the U.S. derivatives markets have seen a number of technological advancements, from physical trading floors to electronic trading platforms.

Now, with blockchain technology, he believes there is an opportunity to further modernize financial market infrastructure without losing regulatory oversight and investor protections.

Notably, there is no technical architecture requirement imposed on derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses under the CFTC's current regulatory framework.

Therefore, firms that leverage blockchain-based networks can apply for regulatory approval under the same set of rules and regulations that apply to traditional financial market participants.

However, Selig also clarified that blockchain adoption is not a license to escape regulatory oversight.

Companies will still need to comply with rules covering anti-money laundering (AML), client protections, market monitoring, risk mitigation and other measures designed to protect the integrity of financial markets.

Simply put, the CFTC is looking to bring blockchain technology into regulated derivatives market infrastructure while maintaining the same standards as traditional financial market participants.

For some time, the CFTC chairman has been pushing for a scenario where U.S. companies developing emerging financial technologies can operate in the country without having to look to international markets.

The latest developments further reinforce the message that the U.S. is open for business for companies building blockchain-based financial market infrastructure, according to Selig.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Malicious JavaScript code snippets were planted on the websites of 178 organizations.

The exploit originated inside Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform, a tool that many large companies use for A/B testing, which means showing users multiple versions of a page to determine which one is more effective.

Report URI estimates that on November 16 the code sat in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely snippets it crawled, and the real number is most likely higher.

Among the websites that could become victims of the hack are some of the largest names in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Fox News, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock. BleepingComputer confirms that the script loads on many of them.

Essentially, the script's goal was to swap a wallet address on the page for the attacker's one, capture card numbers, take screenshots of pages and more. It was a whole stack of tools used to steal personal data, wallets and other assets.

According to Report URI, the attacker's wallets received about $7,040 within the first nine hours. That is a drop in the ocean considering the names involved, though the losses from card skimming are unknown. A card skimmer was added later that day, and a hidden iframe tried to load an iOS exploit chain on older iPhones.

Optimizely confirmed that an unauthorized party had exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation to add malicious JavaScript to certain customer projects. How the flaw worked is yet to be confirmed.

If successful, it could become one of the largest supply-chain attacks we have ever witnessed. Considering the attack came from a third party, we might see one of the largest service migrations in the world, as none of the third-party services and libraries can be trusted nowadays if used through an API.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain tasks to third-party providers all the time, so witnessing a similar situation in our field is more than a possibility.

For product owners: stay cautious and rethink the use of services prone to exploits. For users: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

#5084. Gate Adds GBP and EUR Banking Support for Gate Money via OpenPayd

Home » Exchanges » Gate Adds GBP and EUR Banking Support for Gate Money via OpenPayd

The expanded integration adds virtual pound accounts and euro SEPA rails across Gate’s unified financial platform.

Cryptocurrency and financial services platform Gate has expanded its multi-year partnership with financial infrastructure provider OpenPayd to support the international rollout of Gate Money, its unified fiat, crypto, and equities account.

Under the expanded agreement, Gate is integrating OpenPayd’s British pound (GBP) account infrastructure and euro (EUR) Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payment rails across additional corporate entities.

The expansion builds on a partnership established in 2022, when Gate began using OpenPayd’s virtual IBANs to manage and reconcile European retail and corporate payment flows.

According to the companies, the additional GBP and EUR capabilities will support Gate Money while remaining available across Gate’s broader platform, which serves more than 62 million users worldwide.

The infrastructure expansion follows the October 7, 2026 launch of Gate Money. The product brings digital assets, equities, payments and asset management together within a single account.

Users can hold, receive, transfer, pay and exchange GBP and EUR alongside digital assets, consolidating multiple financial activities within one platform.

The launch represents Gate’s expansion beyond cryptocurrency trading into broader financial services, with fiat payment infrastructure playing a central role in connecting traditional currencies and digital assets.

“Bringing assets, accounts and payments together requires fiat infrastructure that can operate across products and markets,” OpenPayd Chief Commercial Officer Lux Thiagarajah said in a statement.

Gate Founder and CEO Dr. Han said the expanded partnership provides the financial infrastructure needed to integrate Gate’s services and simplify everyday fund management and payments for its global user base.

Gate’s expansion reflects a broader push by crypto exchanges to become all-in-one financial platforms.

Coinbase opened stock and ETF trading to all US users in February, while Kraken and Bybit have expanded into tokenized equities.

Gate announced a crypto-linked Visa card in early October, that is expected to reach more than 40 markets, allowing users to spend their Gate Money balances at merchants. Its broader platform also provides access to metals, indices, forex and commodities, alongside more than 5,400 digital assets and 12,800 stocks and ETFs for trading.

For OpenPayd, the expanded agreement deepens its role in Gate’s financial services operations, strengthening its position as a provider connecting traditional banking with digital assets.

Founded in 2018, OpenPayd offers businesses a range of financial services through a single API, including embedded accounts, foreign exchange, domestic and international payments, Open Banking and stablecoin on- and off-ramps.

The company says it serves more than 1,200 businesses, including eToro, Kraken, OKX and B2C2, and processes over $360 billion in annual transaction volumes.

For London-based OpenPayd, the expanded mandate adds to a growing roster of digital asset clients—including Kraken, OKX, Bybit, eToro, and B2C2—that rely on its API for fiat on/off-ramps and stablecoin settlement.

Seamless fiat banking rails are the missing link for crypto exchanges trying to compete with traditional neobanks as everyday financial hubs. By wiring direct fiat infrastructure into their ecosystem, crypto platforms reduce reliance on third-party workarounds and make it easier for users to hold, convert, and spend traditional currencies alongside crypto and equities.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on Nov. 16, and the proposal lowers the maximum annual issuance of NEAR Protocol from 2.5% to 1.6%. On Tuesday, the price of NEAR dipped to $3.12 in the morning and then went back up to $3.26.

HSP-029 was written by Sal Ternullo, CEO of SVRN, and opened for forum discussion on Oct. 7. The vote closed on Nov. 2, and 99.96% of the veNEAR cast was in favor of the proposal; no veNEAR was cast against it. The Security Council's 14-day window to veto the proposal closed on Nov. 16 with no veto, according to House of Stake.

This is the second inflation cut for NEAR in just over a year. In October 2025, the maximum issuance was halved from the original 5% to 2.5%, and in September 2026, the realized issuance stood at 2.45%, according to HSP-029.

At 1.6%, NEAR will have "one of the lowest annual issuance rates among major blockchains," House of Stake said.

According to House of Stake, the reduction will start one quarter after ratification, and validators still have to adopt the protocol upgrade. The issuance cap will reach 1.6% after 24 months.

Ternullo estimated in HSP-029 that NEAR will avoid issuing 11.8 million tokens over two years. At the current price, these tokens would be worth around $38.5 million.

#5081. Judge Acquits Brothers in $25 Million Ethereum MEV Case After Finding No Proven Wire Fraud

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A Manhattan federal judge has acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno of criminal charges stemming from a 2023 Ethereum trading maneuver that prosecutors said extracted about $25 million. The decision is important, but the takeaway needs precision. It does not amount to judicial approval of every aggressive trading technique on public blockchains. Instead, the judge found that prosecutors failed to prove the material misrepresentations necessary for wire fraud and related convictions in this particular case.

The case concerned maximal extractable value, or MEV, the ability to affect the ordering or inclusion of blockchain transactions for financial gain. Prosecutors said the brothers engineered a bait-and-switch involving Ethereum validator infrastructure and trading bots in April 2023. Their alleged manipulation diverted value that the bots otherwise expected to capture. The defense contested the fraud theory. The unusual technical setting made the case a test of how existing criminal statutes apply to blockchain transactions that may be opportunistic or adversarial but do not necessarily resemble ordinary deceptive financial communications.

US District Judge Jessica Clarke focused on whether the conduct, as charged and proved, met the legal requirements for fraud. According to the ruling reported by Reuters and The Block, the relevant transactions did not involve material false representations of the kind prosecutors needed to establish. The judge distinguished that legal test from the question of whether the behavior was fair, ethical or objectionable. She also noted the absence of a regulated-market rule prohibiting the charged conduct in that setting. An acquittal under particular charges does not pronounce on every possible theory of liability.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Kava Lend collateral exploit.

The brothers were arrested in May 2024, and a jury failed to reach a verdict in November 2025. That sequence matters when interpreting Monday’s ruling: the result followed substantial litigation rather than a quick dismissal immediately after an indictment. The court’s reasoning offers a specific limit on a criminal fraud case, not a complete set of rules for MEV markets. Other facts, jurisdictions or statutory claims could produce different outcomes. Describing the ruling as the legalization of MEV attacks would overstate what the court decided.

MEV remains a practical concern for users who trade on-chain. Transaction ordering, block building and the design of trading bots can affect execution prices and who captures value. Better routing, slippage controls and protocol-level improvements may reduce some forms of extraction, but they do not eliminate competition over transaction priority. Legal certainty matters for developers and traders, while consumer protection remains a separate operational issue. The industry will be watching how prosecutors and policymakers respond to the limits the judge identified.

A ruling on criminal liability also leaves open the technical question of how MEV infrastructure should be designed. Relays, builders and validators can change their software or operational policies, but those changes have different trade-offs for permissionlessness, censorship resistance and execution fairness. Developers can study the facts of this case without treating the acquittal as a blanket endorsement of every form of transaction manipulation. The legal finding is narrower: the government did not prove the fraudulent representation required for the charged offences on the trial record.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Clearpool token-migration safeguards.

The headline is an acquittal in a closely watched federal case, not a blanket safe harbour for exploiting counterparties. For Ethereum users, it reinforces the need to distinguish legal allegations, proven misrepresentations and the technical safeguards available during on-chain execution.

Reporting sources: Reuters reporting on the federal ruling · The Block court report

#5078. Bitcoin Holds $64K After US Bank Outages, but Demand Indicators Flash Warning

Home » Crypto Market News » Bitcoin Holds $64K After US Bank Outages, but Demand Indicators Flash Warning

Calm price action masks deeply negative on-chain demand and a shrinking profit cushion for Bitcoin holders.

Bitcoin price barely reacted to widespread online banking and payment delays across major U.S. banks on Monday, though on-chain data suggests the price stability may mask underlying weakness in demand.

Bitcoin (BTC) edged down 0.2% over the past 24 hours to trade at $64,183 on Tuesday. Crypto market liquidations totaled $278.3 million over the same period—a moderate figure pointing to an absence of forced selling or panic. Bitcoin short liquidations accounted for $88.67 million, according to CoinGlass.

The muted market reaction came despite significant disruptions in traditional US banking infrastructure. According to the Associated Press, a software bug in JPMorgan Chase’s internal systems slowed transaction processing on Monday and triggered ripple effects across the wider banking network.

Customers at several major institutions, including Wells Fargo, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Truist, and Capital One, reported delays, particularly when sending or receiving peer-to-peer transfers via Zelle involving Chase accounts.

While traditional payment rails faced bottlenecks and renewed scrutiny over centralized infrastructure, traders largely treated the incident as a temporary operational hiccup rather than a catalyst to rotate into crypto.

Beneath the calm surface, however, on-chain metrics point to persistent buyer hesitation. A report by CryptoQuant analyst MorenoDV highlights that Bitcoin’s “apparent demand” remains deeply negative.

On November 15, the 30-day reading was around -247,700 BTC, while the one-year figure stood at approximately -1.21 million BTC, with Bitcoin trading near $65,000.

The analyst says the current contraction is among the sharpest negative readings in the period analyzed, with similar levels seen in March 2025 and mid-2026. However, he cautioned that the data does not mean Bitcoin is experiencing an unprecedented collapse or that its price has found a bottom.

What stands out more is how long the weakness has lasted. The 30-day reading has remained mostly negative throughout 2026, with only a brief recovery in late August.

The one-year reading also turned negative around late May and has continued to decline. In other words, short-term improvements in demand have not lasted long enough to signal a sustained recovery.

Bitcoin’s earlier recovery toward $80,000–$85,000 did little to improve the longer-term demand trend. According to MorenoDV, this suggests the rebound lacked strong underlying demand.

The analyst cautions that apparent demand is an indirect on-chain measure, not a direct record of BTC sales or capital outflows. Negative readings have also occurred during previous price recoveries, so the metric cannot reliably predict Bitcoin’s next move.

For a stronger recovery signal, the 30-day reading would need to improve consistently, return above zero and eventually stabilize on the annual measure. Until then, persistent weak demand remains the main concern.

Another on-chain indicator reinforces the cautious outlook. Analyst Axel Adler Jr. reported that the share of Bitcoin supply in profit fell sharply to 52% (down 7% in a week), leaving the market close to an even split between coins held at a profit and those held at a loss.

Meanwhile, long-term holder (LTH) supply fell by 73,900 BTC to 16.2 million BTC, its lowest level in 90 days.

According to Adler, both declines rank among the steepest of the past year, pointing to a shrinking profit cushion and faster redistribution of Bitcoin holdings. The market is now approaching a key threshold: below 50%, more than half of the circulating supply would be held at a loss.

A similar pattern emerged in August 2026, before Bitcoin rebounded by 24%. However, Adler cautions that one historical example is not enough to suggest the same recovery will happen again.

Bitcoin’s stability amid disruptions to traditional banking may suggest resilience, but the on-chain data tells a more cautious story. Persistent negative demand, a declining share of supply in profit and falling long-term holder balances point to weakening market support and a shrinking cushion against further price declines.

#5077. US Supreme Court Turns Down Custodia Bank Appeal Over Federal Reserve Master Account

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Custodia Bank has reached the end of a significant route through the US federal courts in its effort to obtain direct access to Federal Reserve payment services. On November 16, the Supreme Court denied the Wyoming-chartered institution’s petition to review the dispute. The decision leaves a lower-court ruling in place. It is not a fresh opinion deciding every question about crypto-focused banks or an announcement that all such institutions must be kept out of the payments system.

Supreme Court docket 26-62 records a straightforward entry: the petition was denied on November 16, 2026. The justices did not agree to hear oral arguments and issue a merits opinion on the dispute. In practical terms, the lower-court position remains operative, but the denial should not be presented as the Supreme Court affirmatively endorsing each part of the earlier reasoning. This procedural distinction is important. It marks the end of this review attempt while leaving future policy and account-design questions to regulators, lawmakers and separate legal processes.

A Federal Reserve master account gives a qualified institution access to central-bank payment services without depending on another bank for the same connection. Custodia applied through the Kansas City Fed in 2020, arguing that its state bank charter supported its request. The application was denied in January 2023 following disputes over the institution’s business model and the risks the Fed identified. Custodia challenged the outcome, contending that federal law limited the Fed’s discretion. The appellate ruling instead recognised discretion to approve or deny applications in the relevant circumstances.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's crypto licensing proposals.

The banking system is already debating whether some new financial firms should receive narrower forms of direct payments access. A proposed limited or “skinny” account would not necessarily provide the same services or rights as a full master account. That difference matters to institutions building business models around settlement speed, access costs and interest treatment. Even if a different account structure emerges, a future limited product should not be confused with the full access Custodia originally sought. The exact eligibility conditions and supervision requirements will determine whether such designs change the industry materially.

Crypto companies operating as banks or partnering with banks have a commercial interest in dependable dollar settlement, but charter status and payment-system access are not interchangeable. Firms may still use intermediary banking arrangements, with associated concentration and operational risks. The Custodia decision removes one possible path to overturn a prior denial; it does not prohibit new applications or resolve every question about emerging financial infrastructure. The next informative developments will be formal Fed rules, account approvals and the requirements attached to them.

The practical consequence for businesses is continuing uncertainty rather than an abrupt change to payment access. A firm can be licensed at the state level and still face a separate federal assessment of whether it may hold a Reserve Bank account. Policymakers who want to expand access must resolve supervision, settlement risk and eligibility in rules that Reserve Banks can actually apply. Meanwhile, fintech firms may keep using correspondent banks and other intermediaries, with the associated costs and dependencies those arrangements create.

For related context, see our earlier report on custody arrangements for a US bitcoin ETF.

The clearest fact is in the court record: review was denied. Whether the broader US payment system opens new pathways for digital-asset banks depends on future decisions, not on an expansive reading of this one-line order.

Reporting sources: US Supreme Court docket 26-62 · The Block chronology

#5074. Cardano Foundation Seeks Nearly 25 Million ADA for 2027 Events With Token Price Below Budget Assumption

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

A new Cardano community-treasury request raises an awkward budgeting question: what happens when an events programme is priced in dollars but funded in a volatile token? The Cardano Foundation has proposed withdrawing 24,995,775 ADA for a roughly $5 million global conference programme in 2027. Its calculation uses an ADA price of $0.20, while the token was trading nearer $0.15 during Tuesday’s reporting. The proposal is not approved spending, and the difference between those prices is substantial.

The proposed programme covers 12 conferences across multiple regions, with sponsorships, exhibition booths, project participation, travel and associated side events. The Foundation says participating Cardano teams would gain access to shared stands and opportunities to meet developers, partners and prospective users. Of the planned dollar budget, about $2 million relates to sponsorships, with additional material allocations for exhibition equipment, travel and hackathons. This is a marketing and ecosystem-development request to the community treasury, not an investment in a financial asset owned by token holders.

At the assumed price of 20 cents, the requested 24.995 million ADA represents just under $5 million. At 15 cents, the same number of tokens is worth roughly $3.75 million, leaving an indicative shortfall of about $1.25 million. The precise gap will change with the token price and timing of any withdrawal or conversion. The Foundation has indicated that it would operate within the amount actually withdrawn. Delegates therefore need to assess both the strategic case for the programme and how a variable funding base could change its scope.

For related context, see our earlier report on Cardano's Leios scaling development.

Cardano delegated representatives previously rejected funding for the Foundation’s 2026 flagship summit, which was later cancelled. The episode is relevant because governance votes can impose real spending discipline rather than serving as automatic approval for an established institution. The new request follows a separate treasury controversy over a proposal to purchase physical copper. These are distinct decisions, but both show delegates scrutinising what counts as worthwhile use of the community’s assets. A proposal document is not a guarantee that funds will be released.

Conference participation can build relationships and product awareness, yet measuring its return is harder than counting transactions or users. The Foundation has outlined targets for contacts, developer engagement and potential collaborations. Delegates can compare those targets with the cost per event and seek clear reporting on actual results. They can also evaluate whether unspent assets would return to the treasury and whether cost overruns could trigger new requests. The vote will test both confidence in the programme and tolerance for the gap between dollar estimates and ADA-denominated funding.

The debate is also a test of how decentralized treasury decisions are explained. Proposal authors should publish the ADA conversion rate, the dates on which it was calculated, a fiat-cost breakdown, milestone-based disbursements and a clear mechanism for returning unused funds. Voters can then compare expected community reach against alternative uses of scarce treasury assets. Without such measurement, even a successful event is hard to evaluate financially; with it, later proposals can cite more than attendance estimates or social-media impressions.

For related context, see our earlier report on a recent token-holder governance dispute.

This is a live governance choice, not a concluded allocation. The most useful follow-up will be the voting result, any adjusted programme budget and the Foundation’s eventual reporting against its participation targets—not a price forecast based on a single proposal.

Reporting sources: CoinDesk examination of treasury proposal · Crypto.news proposal figures

#5072. 5 Tokens That Held Up Post-TGE

Home » Cryptopedia » 5 Tokens That Held Up Post-TGE

While most crypto tokens struggle to maintain their launch valuations, these five projects have demonstrated varying degrees of post-TGE price resilience.

For almost all crypto tokens, the Token Generation Event (TGE) is the best day they will ever have.

For 2026, so far only about 28% of tokens launched remained above their TGE closing price after 60 days. The median token was trading at just 0.64x its launch close.

Tokens surviving and rising in price for days, hours, and even minutes post-launch is not an easy feat. Here are five tokens that have so far avoided the typical post-TGE collapse:

Today, $1WIN is trading around $0.045, roughly 50% above its public sale price.

It is too early to compare that performance with tokens that have been trading for months or years. What makes $1WIN worth paying attention to is that its held steady in the post-TGE price rise and has a big business behind it. 1win has operated since 2016 with 100 million players and its gaming business is profitable independently of the token.

The company also plans revenue-funded open-market buybacks, while 10% of $1WIN spent through supported products will be burned. Supply is capped at one billion tokens with no additional minting.

Hyperliquid’s HYPE remains one of the clearest examples of a token that did considerably more than survive launch.

HYPE began trading in 2024 and today is hitting over $73, leaving it several multiples above its earliest market prices nearly two years later.

The underlying exchange also gives the token an economic connection to platform activity. Trading fees flow into Hyperliquid’s Assistance Fund, which acquires HYPE, with accumulated tokens subsequently burned.

That combination of product usage, revenue and token demand makes HYPE one of the stronger examples of the kind of pre-TGE traction highlighted in Decasonic’s research.

Aster launched ASTER in September 2025 as the token behind its decentralized spot and perpetuals trading platform.

Despite substantial volatility since then, ASTER was trading around $0.65. It remains well below its $2.42 all-time high, but also far above its earliest trading levels.

ASTER has not gone up in a straight line. But more than a year after launch, the token has retained a substantial part of the value created during its early growth rather than fading toward zero after TGE.

Backpack’s BP demonstrates another type of post-TGE resilience.

The token launched in March and subsequently fell as low as roughly $0.12 in May. By this month, BP had recovered to around $0.90, after reaching an all-time high of $1.66 in October.

That makes BP interesting because its strength did not come immediately after TGE. The token went through a deep early correction before rebuilding.

It also sits inside an established exchange and wallet ecosystem, with utility including trading-fee discounts, rewards, staking and access to other Backpack products.

ZAMA is trading around $0.067, approximately one-third above that public auction price.

The token also has direct utility within the Zama Protocol, where it is used to pay for encryption and decryption services and reward operators and stakers securing the network.

Stronger 2026 launches generally arrived with real usage, paying users, revenue, TVL or another measurable source of pre-TGE traction. The token was being added to something that already worked.

A strong launch can be created by hype. Holding up once the launch is over usually requires much more.

#5070. Solana Drops “Mainnet Beta” Label as Foundation Introduces Protocol Version 1.0

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Solana is retiring a label that has accompanied the blockchain since its launch: “mainnet beta.” In a November 16 announcement, the Solana Foundation introduced protocol version 1.0 and said the network should now be described simply as mainnet. It is a meaningful coordination change for developers and operators, but the Foundation was also explicit about what it is not. Users do not need to move funds, update token addresses or assume that a new feature has suddenly been enabled.

Solana has operated as a live production network for years while retaining the beta designation. Removing that wording is not a chain migration, hard reset or new issuance event. Accounts, SOL balances, applications and historical transactions remain on the same network, according to the Foundation. This matters for holders who may encounter posts suggesting they must claim a replacement token or connect a wallet to an upgrade portal. There is no such user requirement in the announcement. The change concerns how the live protocol is named and described.

The more technical development is a shared protocol version that is separate from the software version of any one validator client. Solana infrastructure includes Agave and Firedancer implementations, and those releases have their own numbering schemes. A network-level protocol number can make it clearer which clients support a given set of protocol rules, reducing reliance on one implementation as the reference point. That is coordination infrastructure rather than a substitute for testing. Validators still need to follow release notes and compatibility instructions for the specific software they deploy.

For related context, see our earlier report on recent Solana developer and validator updates.

A common protocol designation makes future network changes easier to communicate across independent implementations and tools. It could also help documentation, explorers and service providers describe compatibility consistently. But the Foundation cautioned that announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement in one step. Feature activations and software rollouts retain their own schedules and technical requirements. Claims that Solana 1.0 instantly adds a particular throughput increase, fee mechanism or transaction feature should therefore be checked against separate activation notices.

For applications and RPC providers, the near-term work is keeping technical references current and watching client release guidance. For everyday users, the main practical change may simply be seeing “mainnet” rather than “mainnet beta” in wallets or interfaces. The market may attach symbolic significance to the milestone, but label changes are not a reliable stand-in for uptime, decentralisation, performance or adoption. Those outcomes still need to be measured independently as the network evolves.

Protocol labels are useful only if developers can connect them to concrete compatibility guarantees. Projects that integrate wallets, exchanges and payment systems still need to test RPC behavior, client changes and transaction-handling assumptions against real releases. Validators likewise need to monitor operator guidance instead of interpreting '1.0' as a permanent freeze in features or risk. A shared versioning convention may make upgrades easier to communicate, but sustained performance and reliable incident response remain the evidence users ultimately experience.

Solana 1.0 is best understood as a naming and versioning milestone. It establishes a common language for the protocol while leaving the hard work of shipping, activating and measuring future improvements to the network’s normal processes.

Reporting sources: Solana Foundation announcement
