#5068. Tokenized stocks are exactly where stablecoins were in 2020 – How?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Stablecoins started as a way to hold dollars on-chain. Then people started lending, trading, and earning with them. In time, DeFi grew up around them.

Tokenized stocks are heading down the same route now, and the resemblance is uncanny.

What’s worth noting here is how much of it is actually being used.

According to data from Token Terminal, tokenized stocks deposited into DeFi are now worth about $300 million. A year ago, that was at approx. $12.5 million.

This number didn’t move at all through late 2025. Things picked up in the spring, blasted through $100 million by around August, and then shot past a quarter million in September.

It’s also a bigger share of the market now. That $300 million is 6.3% of the $4.8 billion tokenized stock market cap. Last year, only 2.4% was being put to work.

Because once they’re there, holders can borrow against them, earn fees by providing liquidity, or chase yield.

And every new way to use them, is essentially one more reason not to cash out.

Tokenized stocks now have a market cap of about $4.8 billion. Stablecoins crossed that exact number in March 2020. Since then, stablecoins have grown, 59 times over! The number is at $285 billion now.

Tokenized stocks are moving fast too. They were worth only a few tens of millions in early 2025.

But why? A blockchain is basically a ledger for assets, and it gets more useful when it holds things people really want. U.S Stocks are about as in-demand as it gets.

Stablecoins didn’t get to where they are without the effort.

They made it through the COVID crash, the Terra collapse, FTX, and the USDC de-peg after SVB failed. Market cap fell by 28% between February 2022 and October 2023, then spiked up to a high by September 2024.

What kept them going though? Cash and T-bill reserves backed every token, plus people who actually wanted to use them.

Tokenized stocks follow the same 1:1 idea.

Except the risk factor is higher. So is the potential for gains.

Hardware-wallet maker Trezor has disclosed a breach at shipping partner Skladon affecting data connected with approximately 27,000 customer orders. The incident is serious because a delivery address and product purchase history can reveal who may own crypto. It is also important not to turn a data-exposure story into a false claim that customer wallets were drained. Trezor says its own systems were not compromised, and the disclosed records did not include wallet backups, PINs or passphrases.

Trezor says Skladon informed it on November 15 of unauthorized access linked to an incident on November 7. The data at issue concerned orders placed between August 9 and November 7, 2026. The company estimates roughly 27,000 affected orders and says the investigation is continuing. The records included names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses and information about orders and products bought. A limited number of earlier August customers may also have been affected even though their information had been anonymized within Trezor’s own systems before the notification process.

Someone with a buyer’s name, address and exact device order can craft a convincing phishing message or impersonate customer support. The same combination may create physical-security concerns if a criminal believes the household controls valuable assets. None of this requires compromising the hardware wallet’s cryptographic security. Trezor says it never requests wallet recovery data by telephone and warns affected users to treat unexpected calls, texts, emails and letters with suspicion. If a message uses authentic order details, that does not make its instructions legitimate.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet-key incident.

The company says it has contacted affected customers it can still reach and notified a data-protection authority. It is introducing or expanding anonymous pickup at collection points in much of Europe, reducing the amount of residential delivery information involved in future orders. Trezor also says it is working to shorten customer-data retention from 90 to 45 days, with further reductions under consideration. Those steps address the long-term exposure of operational records rather than claiming that a damaged secret key can be repaired after the fact.

Customers should go directly to the vendor’s known website for official support rather than follow contact details supplied in an unsolicited message. They should never type a recovery phrase into a web form or share it with a caller. Buyers can also consider whether their delivery address and household security require extra attention. Anyone receiving threats should contact appropriate local authorities. The precise number of affected people, rather than orders, may differ, and the final breach scope may change as investigators establish what was exported.

A legitimate package or delivery notice is especially convincing because it can refer to a real order. Criminals might use the information for emails, texts, calls or fraudulent web pages that look like shipping support. Wallet owners should be wary of any message that asks them to type a recovery phrase, install a replacement wallet application or approve an unexpected transaction. Those requests are unrelated to normal delivery updates. The strongest precaution is to verify a message through a separately opened official website, not by following a link in the message itself.

For related context, see our earlier report on Coinbase's discussion of cold-storage controls.

#5063. How Bitcoin still competes with a 2.92% Treasury yield after inflation

The headline 10-year Treasury yield fell on Nov. 16, while its inflation-adjusted counterpart edged up and remained 29 basis points above its Nov. 6 level.

The 10-year Treasury yield after inflation rose to 2.92% on Monday, Nov. 16, up 29 basis points since Nov. 6. The move left Bitcoin competing with that yield even as the headline 10-year Treasury rate fell.

Treasury’s nominal yield data showed a decline to 5.12% from 5.15% on Friday, Nov. 13, a three-basis-point move. Its real-yield series moved the other way, edging up one basis point from 2.91%.

The real yield had stood at 2.63% on Nov. 6. The 29-basis-point rise therefore spans multiple sessions, with Monday adding only one basis point.

Bitcoin provides no contractual interest income. A higher yield on inflation-protected government debt can therefore raise the opportunity cost of holding it: investors have a stronger income alternative against which to weigh Bitcoin’s potential returns and volatility.

The 2.92% figure is also a long-term Treasury curve benchmark, not an overnight borrowing rate or a promised return for every investor. Treasury estimates its constant-maturity nominal and real par yields from indicative market quotations. An investor’s realized return on a particular bond can differ.

The November 16 bond rally lowered the nominal benchmark while the 10-year real yield reached 2.92%. Compare Monday’s small move with the rise since November 6.

Monday added one basis point to the real yield.

The real yield rose 29 basis points across multiple sessions.

The real-yield hurdle did not ease on Monday; its 29-basis-point rise spans November 6–16.

Curve estimates use indicative quotations. The calculated spread includes inflation risk and liquidity effects; it is not a pure forecast. The graphic establishes no Bitcoin price response. Comparisons are dated observations, not intraday moves.

Inputs are dated 10-year Treasury par yields. Spread = nominal minus real: 5.15−2.91=2.24 pp; 5.12−2.92=2.20 pp. Monday changes: real +1 bp, spread −4 bp, nominal −3 bp. Since Nov. 6: 2.92−2.63=0.29 pp=29 bp. Bars start at zero; both real-yield comparison views share a labelled 2.60%–3.00% scale.

Curve estimates use indicative quotations. The calculated spread includes inflation risk and liquidity effects; it is not a pure forecast. The graphic establishes no Bitcoin price response. Comparisons are dated observations, not intraday moves.

A simple subtraction of Treasury’s real par yield from its nominal par yield gives a spread of 2.20 percentage points on Monday, down from 2.24 on Friday. The four-basis-point narrowing explains how the nominal benchmark could fall while the real benchmark rose.

The spread is often described as inflation compensation. But the Federal Reserve’s explanation shows why it cannot be read as a pure inflation forecast: it also reflects compensation for inflation risk and differences in liquidity between nominal Treasuries and inflation-protected securities. The subtraction alone cannot show which component drove Monday’s change.

Historical research supports caution about the transmission to crypto. The authors of a 2023 IMF working paper found that U.S. monetary tightening reduced a broad crypto price factor through investor risk-taking. Their study does not estimate how Monday’s one-basis-point real-yield move affected Bitcoin.

Watch the inflation-adjusted Treasury yield for signs that competition from bonds is easing. The headline rate can fall while that yield stays elevated.

South Korean financial app Toss is preparing a built-in wallet that could make sending cryptocurrencies feel more like using an ordinary payments contact list. Local reports cited by crypto.news say the first release will support ether, Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC on Ethereum, with a rollout planned for the week of November 16. The platform has roughly 30 million registered users, though that figure must not be confused with 30 million wallet customers or a prediction of adoption.

The proposed Toss Coin Wallet would appear within the Assets area of the company’s established app. Users would be able to create a wallet, view balances, deposit supported assets and make transfers without first downloading a separate crypto-specific product. Reports describe contact-based sending that reduces the need to copy long addresses manually. That interface convenience does not change the underlying Ethereum transfer: moving ETH or stablecoins remains an on-chain operation, with network fees and irreversible settlement characteristics. The feature’s actual adoption will depend on customer onboarding and reliable day-to-day use, not simply the size of Toss’s existing registration base.

Toss has characterized the wallet as noncustodial, meaning it will not hold the assets on the customer’s behalf as an exchange typically would. The practical details of key management, recovery and account safeguards will therefore be important to examine once the product is live. Transactions will still require Ethereum gas payments even if Toss does not levy a separate platform transfer fee. Users also need to understand that a token sent to the wrong network or incompatible address can be hard or impossible to recover. A simplified contact screen should be evaluated alongside the security controls beneath it.

For related context, see our earlier report on stablecoin-supply and liquidity trends.

The initial version described in reporting is about holding and transferring three digital assets. It is not an announced exchange for buying crypto with Korean won, nor a completed stablecoin checkout integration across Toss merchants. The distinction matters because mobile finance applications can offer very different forms of crypto access, from payment rails to brokerage services. Toss has separately explored stablecoin payments and other blockchain infrastructure with partners, but exploratory pilots should not be counted as services already available to all customers.

South Korea’s policy discussion on domestically issued won-backed stablecoins is still developing. The Toss wallet’s initial lineup instead uses ether and existing dollar-pegged stablecoins. For regulators, the questions will include consumer disclosures, anti-money-laundering compliance and who is responsible when a user needs assistance. For competitors, the more immediate test is whether ordinary financial apps can make self-custody accessible without creating confusion over fees, network selection and support. Watch the live release notes rather than assuming every previously discussed partnership has launched together.

The important commercial questions concern the exact custody and onboarding model, not simply the size of Toss's existing customer base. A noncustodial wallet can bring new users on-chain, but those users still need access to funds, recovery tools, regulatory disclosures and reliable transaction support. USDT and USDC are dollar-linked assets with issuer and banking dependencies. If the product is launched as described, its adoption will be measured more usefully in funded wallets and sustained activity than in the total count of people who use the broader finance app.

If Toss delivers the described experience, it would be a distribution experiment for stablecoins on a major consumer platform. The sensible comparison is not registered app users versus crypto traders but activated wallets, successfully completed transfers and the controls offered when something goes wrong.

His central argument: extreme selling pressure may signal an opportunity, even as XRP price trades below $1 and investors remain deeply fearful.

The most striking figure comes from Crypto Insight UK: an XRP daily RSI of 16.17, described as its lowest in a decade. Matt acknowledges the limitation directly: “Just because we’re oversold doesn’t mean we can’t go lower.”

The weekly chart offers a less straightforward signal. Citing analyst D Greg Crypto, Matt describes XRP’s weekly RSI falling below 20, recovering that level and then quickly testing it again—an unusually compressed sequence compared with previous recoveries.

Matt also highlights Charting Guy’s view that XRP resembles a previous cycle’s bottoming process, with a weekly bullish divergence and a possible re-accumulation pattern. That analyst maintains a minimum xrp price target of $4.36, not a forecast for the eventual peak.

The timing is considerably less certain. Charting Guy suggests possible altcoin seasons in summer 2027 and late 2028, while Matt argues that Bitcoin’s direction will remain important for XRP and the wider market.

Matt’s own response is to keep holding rather than trade the volatility. He identifies himself as an enthusiast without a financial background, not a financial adviser.

For now, the consequential question is whether exhausted selling develops into sustained buying. Moon Lambo presents several arguments for recovery, but its own weekly-RSI discussion leaves a clear risk unresolved: XRP price could remain under pressure before any broader market rebound takes hold.

A new connection between the Solflare wallet and MoneyGram Ramps aims to solve a practical stablecoin problem: a user can hold digital dollars on Solana but still need physical cash. MoneyGram says eligible Solflare users can now withdraw USDC as local currency at participating agent locations in more than 170 countries and territories. That geographic coverage is substantial, but it should not be read as an unconditional cash-out guarantee in every location or for every customer.

According to MoneyGram’s November 16 announcement, a Solflare user selects Withdraw, chooses MoneyGram, enters an amount of USDC and follows the guided payout process before collecting cash from a participating outlet. The integration links a self-custody wallet to a familiar physical distribution network. There is still a distinction between initiating a blockchain transfer and receiving funds at the counter: identity verification, local availability and payout requirements can affect completion. Users should rely on the official flow for quotes, instructions and confirmation rather than sending tokens to an address received in an unsolicited message.

MoneyGram is promoting zero cash-out fees for eligible Solflare users through December 31, 2026. That is a time-limited offer, not a permanent commitment that every step of a stablecoin withdrawal will be free of all possible costs. Network charges, exchange-rate effects or local requirements may be relevant to a particular transaction, and the published terms and quote should control. The ability to convert tokens into spendable local currency is likely to matter more to many users than a headline about blockchain throughput alone.

For related context, see our earlier report on the latest stablecoin-liquidity developments.

Stablecoins move value across digital networks, but they are not universally accepted as a way to pay everyday expenses. MoneyGram’s retail footprint provides a bridge for customers who need banknotes or a locally familiar cash service. The company says its Ramps business has grown substantially and is now being integrated with additional wallets. This arrangement could help cross-border recipients, freelancers or travelers, although actual savings compared with traditional remittance routes will vary by jurisdiction, payment size and the available alternatives.

Solflare users retain control of assets in their wallets before initiating a withdrawal, but redeeming those assets involves a service provider and its compliance procedures. That division should be explained clearly to avoid suggesting that a physical cash payout happens without intermediaries. MoneyGram is responsible for relevant payout operations, while the wallet provides access to the flow. The network’s permissionless transfer capabilities and the retail service’s regulated customer requirements are separate parts of the experience. Product reliability will be measured by the success rate of that handoff.

Coverage in a country does not guarantee that every local counter offers the same payout currency, opening hours or amount limits. A traveller should confirm eligibility, identification rules, transaction size, charges and whether the specific location participates before sending any digital asset. Unlike a regular card or bank withdrawal, an on-chain transfer can be irreversible even if a cash pickup is delayed. Clear status messages, refund procedures and support channels will therefore be as important to the product's reputation as the geographical scope of the partner network.

For related context, see our earlier report on a tokenized settlement trial by central banks.

The launch is a concrete use case for dollar stablecoins rather than a broad forecast about adoption. Its significance will depend on where customers can actually collect cash, the all-in cost after promotions end and whether the service remains dependable during high demand.

#5057. JPMorgan and DBS offer 24/7 dollar transfers… without stablecoins

Institutional clients can move dollars between the US and Singapore around the clock. One JPMorgan conversion step still pauses for three hours on Saturdays.

Singapore bank DBS and JPMorgan's blockchain business Kinexys have connected their blockchain-based dollar accounts in Singapore and the US, allowing institutional clients to transfer funds instantly around the clock as an alternative to stablecoins, according to DBS's Nov. 16 announcement.

The service gives corporate treasurers another way to move bank deposits beyond traditional banking hours.

Ant International is the first client of the commercially ready connection, which uses Partior to coordinate settlement between the banks' permissioned networks. The launch puts a practical service behind the interoperability framework the banks announced in November 2025.

The competitive opportunity for banks is to make deposits easier to move while preserving the customer relationship attached to them.

Stablecoins offer another way to transfer dollars digitally, but whether companies favor one route depends on where they can send the money, how they recover cash, and what the whole transaction costs.

A tokenized deposit represents a bank deposit, while USDC is issued by Circle affiliates and backed by cash and cash-equivalent reserves. Moving either on a blockchain does not make the customer's counterparty or redemption arrangements identical.

DBS says transfers within Kinexys's Blockchain Deposit Account network operate 24/7/365. However, moving money between those accounts and traditional demand-deposit accounts has a maintenance interruption every Saturday from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern Time.

The banks did not disclose fees or how much cash Ant needs to keep on hand, so companies have no like-for-like cost comparison with stablecoin transfers.

Circle says standard banking-rail USDC redemptions can be free and typically settle in up to two business days, while qualifying Circle Platform and Circle Payments Network customers can obtain free near-real-time redemption.

Circle attributes fast redemption to cash pre-positioned at bank partners, which earns less than Treasuries, and its Mint product terms also make instant settlement conditional on participating banks offering it.

Direct Mint access is restricted to eligible institutions, while individuals obtain USDC through exchanges and wallets.

A Bank for International Settlements (BIS) working paper published Oct. 13 uses weekly US data from January 2019 through June 2025. Researchers Rashad Ahmed and Iñaki Aldasoro found that higher deposit rates were followed by slower stablecoin growth, and that the relationship was stronger for USDC than USDT.

The paper links a one-standard-deviation increase in deposit repricing to about 2.4 percentage points slower stablecoin growth over ten weeks. Stablecoin growth averaged 15% over a ten-week period in the sample.

The findings suggest that deposit pricing helps shape demand for stablecoins, but the authors say their analysis does not establish that stablecoin growth necessarily reduces total bank deposits or lending.

The DBS link is part of a wider effort to make bank money usable across more systems, though the products are distinct.

On Oct. 19, JPMorgan brought its JPM Coin deposit token to Ethereum, alongside Base, for institutional clients. That public-chain token is separate from the permissioned Blockchain Deposit Account network connected to DBS.

Using its internal data, JPMorgan reported more than $4 trillion in cumulative transactions and $7 billion in average daily volume across the broader Kinexys platform.

In September, DBS said it and Citi's New York office had completed a dollar payment via SWIFT Digital Ledger in minutes over a weekend.

Separately, The Clearing House selected Quant to support a tokenized-deposit network with connections to RTP and CHIPS. Participating institutions are expected to gain access in the first half of 2027.

A faster transfer inside one network only helps if the receiving bank can accept it.

The competition is consequently about more than whose blockchain runs all weekend. The decisive advantage for corporate cash would be money available where it is needed, with fewer costly balances waiting elsewhere.

Pixel Tap is a cyberpunk combat-themed mini-game where players can tap the screen to earn in-game coins, upgrade robot fighters, and take part in real-time battles against each other. It is part of the wider Pixelverse ecosystem, and the game revolves around tapping mechanics and PvP battles.

In-game currency can be earned through referrals, daily tasks, battles, and general activity. Players can get into battles and earn points and tokens in PvE and PvP settings. $PIXFI is the native token of the platform, and rewards can be earned in it.

Players can earn the token through the play-to-earn model and also by taking part in airdrops and boss raids. There are community events that help players interact with each other as well.

Telegram games give an easy and convenient way for players to engage with a lot of these tap-to-earn apps. They started out as simple games and have evolved into much more complex ecosystems of their own overtime, offering a wide variety of gaming experience.

Each game brings something different and can be appealing to a different type of gamer. However, it is advisable to do your own reseach before monetarily investing in any game.

#5054. Ripple CTO Emeritus Reveals Why XRP Took BTC’s Code

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Ripple CTO Emeritus Reveals Why XRP Took BTC’s Code

Here’s why XRP’s Ledger still supports the original elliptic curve that Bitcoin uses for signatures.

David Schwartz, Ripple’s CTO Emeritus and one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger, explained a deliberate early design choice this week.

Responding to a post about the ledger’s technical roots, he wrote: “We did things that way in the very early days because we didn’t want to face potential criticism that our choices of those core crypto functions were less secure than bitcoin’s.”

The discussion began with XRPL validator Vet, who noted that the ledger’s earliest code included helper functions and comments from Bitcoin’s original client, written by Satoshi Nakamoto and copied by early developer Jed McCaleb.

Did you know all of us on the XRP Ledger use design choices by Satoshi daily?15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Satoshi wrote.Jed copied Satoshi's timekeeping code into the XRPL, including… pic.twitter.com/IZOaa4w0bz

Most of that code was removed by the end of 2014; in December of that year, then-engineering lead Nik Bougalis deleted the last of the timekeeping routines along with one of Satoshi’s comments.

Two design choices remain. The XRP Ledger still supports the secp256k1 elliptic curve that Bitcoin uses for signatures (it also supports the newer Ed25519 curve, so not every account relies on secp256k1).

Separately, every XRPL address is still generated the Bitcoin way: the public key is hashed with SHA-256 and then with RIPEMD-160 before encoding. Those steps are used by every account on the network today.

David Schwartz’s explanation is straightforward. In the network’s first years, the team preferred to reuse cryptographic primitives already proven in Bitcoin rather than introduce untested alternatives that crypto critics, particularly in the Bitcoin community, could attack as weaker or experimental.

We did things that way in the very early days because we didn't want to face potential criticism that our choices of those core crypto functions were less secure than bitcoin's.

Using the same curve and address-generation method removed one potential line of criticism before it could be raised. Ripple CTO Emeritus has noted it is impossible to know whether different choices would actually have drawn that criticism; the point was to avoid having to defend the cryptography at all.

The early code sharing was limited and temporary. The consensus mechanism, transaction model, and most of the ledger’s architecture were built independently.

It's hard to say. Obviously, we never got those criticisms. But it's hard to know if we would have. I'm not sure we would have come up with better ones had we made our own decisions anyway.

What survived are two well-understood cryptographic building blocks that have remained secure and widely implemented for more than a decade. Later additions, including Ed25519 support, gave users and developers additional options without removing the original path.

The exchange is a small window into how the XRP Ledger was constructed: deliberately conservative on core cryptography in its first years, then gradually cleaned of borrowed code once the project had its footing. The two pieces are still in daily use by everyone on-chain.

#5053. CoW Swap Adds Native Solana Trading With Solver Auctions and a One-Year Volume-Fee Waiver

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

CoW Swap has launched an alpha that allows traders to start and finish asset swaps on Solana, extending an intent-based model previously associated with Ethereum. The basic difference is worth understanding: rather than manually choosing a route and submitting a conventional swap, users sign an instruction that competing solvers try to execute at acceptable terms. CoW DAO is also waiving its own volume fee on Solana for at least a year, a decision that should not be mistaken for the disappearance of all trading costs.

Before this release, CoW Swap could facilitate certain routes into Solana from Ethereum-compatible networks. The new alpha supports trades whose starting and ending assets are on Solana itself. That is a different proposition for applications already serving Solana users. The launch includes an integration with lending platform Kamino and access to a solver network that CoW DAO describes as comprising more than 30 participants. The alpha designation also matters: traders should check supported assets, order conditions and current operational limitations before assuming every feature available on other chains is identical.

With an intent-based order, a trader specifies the assets and the price or conditions they will accept. Solvers can compete to find a matching trade or route liquidity through available venues. CoW Swap says its batching and execution design can help reduce opportunities for certain sandwich attacks and avoid some failed on-chain swaps. That is a design objective, not a guarantee that every order will fill at the best imaginable price. Market depth, slippage, solver incentives and latency still shape outcomes, especially for thinly traded tokens.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana confidentiality infrastructure.

CoW DAO says it will waive its own Solana volume fee for at least the first 12 months. Users should distinguish that platform charge from the economic costs of crossing bid-ask spreads, securing liquidity and potentially using network resources. Sponsored transactions can also change who pays an upfront network fee without making trade execution economically costless. The order’s displayed execution price and the eventual tokens received remain the meaningful comparison with other venues. Fee promotions are useful, but not a substitute for checking route quality.

Solana already has active trading infrastructure, so the question is not whether CoW Swap brings decentralized exchanges to a previously empty market. It is whether solver competition and order batching create a sufficiently different experience to attract liquidity and integrations. For lending applications, a reliable swap path can also affect liquidation and portfolio-management workflows. Independent measurements of fills, failed attempts, spreads and protection against adverse ordering will be more persuasive than the cumulative trade-volume figures of the protocol’s older networks.

Execution quality needs independent measurement. Users comparing an intent-based solver with a traditional aggregator should examine the final amount received after all network and protocol costs, the time needed to settle and how failed or partially filled routes are handled. The headline fee waiver should not obscure transaction costs or liquidity-provider economics that may still apply. Solana's faster settlement can improve the experience, but it does not by itself guarantee that every swap will beat a direct exchange quote under volatile market conditions.

For related context, see our earlier report on a recent DeFi market-security case.

The launch adds another execution model to Solana, not a guarantee against losses or manipulation. Users should treat an alpha product’s safeguards and fee arrangements as claims to verify through its documentation and trading results as adoption grows.

#5051. Hyperliquid’s $3.4 billion HYPE burn machine faces new test as USDC reserves shrink

Trading volume surged nearly 16%, but a 7.8% decline in USDC supply raises questions about the sustainability of a second source of HYPE buyback funding.

Hyperliquid's perpetual futures trading volume surged nearly 16% over the past week, even as the network's USDC holdings declined, exposing competing trends in the revenue streams supporting HYPE token buybacks.

Data from DeFiLlama showed that the decentralized exchange processed $75.72 billion in perpetual futures transactions over the seven days ending Nov. 16, an increase of 15.87%.

However, USDC capitalization on the network fell 7.76% to $6.02 billion during the same period. The stablecoin accounted for approximately 98.85% of Hyperliquid's total stablecoin supply.

The divergence puts Hyperliquid's token-buyback model in focus, particularly as the protocol increasingly relies on both trading fees and income generated from stablecoin reserves to support HYPE purchases.

Hyperliquid has already accumulated about 49.03 million HYPE tokens through its Assistance Fund, representing 4.9% of the cryptocurrency's initial one-billion-token supply.

Under the protocol's rules, the holdings were treated as burned and were valued at about $3.37 billion as of Nov. 17. Their estimated acquisition cost was $1.45 billion, with an average purchase price near $29.50 per token.

Hyperliquid's fee structure directs trading revenue toward liquidity providers, market deployers, and the Assistance Fund, which automatically converts its allocated fees into HYPE.

Weekly turnover rose while chain-wide USDC fell. The routes to HYPE purchases depend on different balances, rates and timing.

Actual fee receipts and reserve payments are the comparable inputs for assessing HYPE funding.

This mechanism has become an important component of HYPE's token economics, with the protocol using revenue from its trading business to steadily accumulate tokens.

The latest increase in perpetuals volume strengthens one side of that arrangement by expanding the trading activity from which fees are collected.

However, the amount reaching the Assistance Fund also depends on transaction fee tiers, staking discounts, maker rebates and revenue-sharing arrangements with market deployers.

Hyperliquid has also expanded its funding model beyond trading fees through AQAv2, an arrangement that redirects income earned on eligible USDC reserves toward the protocol.

Under the framework, Hyperliquid receives approximately 90% of cost-adjusted reserve yield, providing another source of funds for HYPE purchases.

Coinbase serves as the treasury operator, while Circle provides technical support for the stablecoin infrastructure.

Unlike trading fees, which depend on transaction activity, this income is tied to qualifying USDC balances and prevailing interest rates.

That creates a potential vulnerability as stablecoin capitalization declines, even while activity on the exchange strengthens.

The importance of Hyperliquid's stablecoin reserves became more apparent in the third quarter, when the network began generating substantial income through the AQAv2 arrangement.

According to Bitwise and Allium, the protocol accrued approximately $17.26 million in USDC reserve income during the quarter, including $14.86 million in September.

At the end of September, Hyperliquid held approximately $7.35 billion in total USDC, with $6.77 billion backing HyperCore, its trading infrastructure. Of that amount, the treasury held approximately $6.09 billion.

Using those balances and a 3.22% annual reference rate, Bitwise estimated the arrangement could generate about $16.09 million over 30 days, or nearly $196 million annually.

That potential income adds another source of demand for HYPE, reinforcing the buybacks already funded by trading fees.

The latest contraction in USDC capitalization threatens to weaken that contribution if the decline extends to the qualifying reserves on which the income is earned.

The reserve arrangement calculates revenue from daily balances and interest rates over 30-day periods, with payments reaching the Assistance Fund eight days after each period ends.

Consequently, shrinking eligible reserves would gradually reduce the income available for HYPE purchases, while stronger trading activity could help compensate through higher fee collections.

For Hyperliquid, the emerging tension is between an increasingly active derivatives business and a contracting stablecoin base that supports a separate source of buyback funding.

The next reserve-income distribution will provide a clearer picture of whether Hyperliquid can sustain this additional source of HYPE demand as USDC balances fall.

#5050. Satoshi-Era Bitcoin Holder Wakes Up After 15 Years, Refuting $250 Billion ‘Lost’ Claim

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

A Bitcoin address that had not moved coins since February 2011 transferred 75 BTC on Nov. 17, according to Galaxy Research. At the current price of $64,935 per BTC, the coins are worth around $4.87 million.

The address is listed as a defendant in a $250 billion lawsuit in New York Supreme Court, in which the plaintiffs are trying to have early Bitcoin wallets declared "lost." Galaxy Research said that several other addresses from the same list have also moved coins in 2026.

According to Galaxy Research analysts, early on Nov. 17, in block 976,209, the address 1ALpEWtXApR19hLXvcG8NfkPyGsUMhFPMS sent coins for the first time. It was first funded on Feb. 8, 2011. At that time, Bitcoin was trading at about $0.90. After 15.8 years, the coins went to an unknown address with a 399-satoshi fee, or about 26 cents, for a paper gain of more than 7,000,000%.

Onchain databases list the wallet as Noah Doe #3409 (Salomon Client Dusted). That label is how it ended up among the defendants in the high-profile case ABC Company, XYZ Company, and Noah Doe v. John Does 1–39,069.

According to the lawsuit, an anonymous plaintiff using the pseudonym Noah Doe and two companies want the rights to 39,069 Bitcoin wallets that have not moved coins for more than five years. The plaintiffs said that these wallets hold about 3.8 million BTC, and at the current price, the coins are worth around $250 billion.

The plaintiffs filed the lawsuit under New York's lost-and-found law, Article 7-B of the Personal Property Law. Under the law, a person who finds lost property has to give it to the police, and the property goes to the finder if the owner does not claim it in time. In the lawsuit, the plaintiffs valued each address at less than $10, and they argued that the waiting period for such items was one year.

They "found" dormant addresses with an algorithm, saved them onto USB flash drives and took them to the New York Police Department (NYPD). Then they served the owners on the blockchain, through microtransactions with embedded messages (OP_RETURN). The practice is known as "dusting," and the campaign is tied to Salomon Brothers Strategic Advisors. Once the waiting period ran out, the plaintiffs asked the court to recognize the coins as theirs.

The case has been put on hold several times over motions to dismiss and amicus curiae briefs from outside experts. At a hearing on Sept. 8, the Bitcoin Policy Institute asked to intervene as a defendant, and The Digital Chamber asked to join the case as amicus curiae. Galaxy Research described it as a case "in which anonymous plaintiffs are seeking to claim legal title over Satoshi's coins."

Galaxy Research's Will Owens, who attended the hearing, said that The Digital Chamber's arguments were "well pleaded" and that "the judge sounded sympathetic to them."

Critics of the lawsuit argue that Article 7-B was written for things you can pick up and hand over for safekeeping. It wasn't written for blockchain records when the "finder" doesn't hold the private keys.

In September, Galaxy head of research Alex Thorn also said that the Lost and Found Property Law includes "protection from 'Noah Doe-style' dormancy attacks on legal ownership."

#5049. Bitwise Maps Solana to $80, $385 or $1,100 by 2031 in Scenario-Based Research

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Bitwise has published a five-year framework for Solana that includes very different possible outcomes for SOL’s price. The range extends from an $80 bear case to a $385 base case and an $1,100 bullish scenario for 2031, according to reporting on its November 16 research. Those numbers are scenarios, not an announcement that the token will reach any particular level. The interesting story is the set of expectations about tokenized securities, payments and on-chain trading required to justify the more ambitious outcome.

Bitwise’s paper, “Tokenization, 24/7 Trading, and the Economics of Solana,” links possible SOL valuations to the role a fast blockchain might play in financial activity. The firm argues that tokenized assets, payments and round-the-clock trading could shift more transactions on-chain over time. Its publicly available summary identifies a $385 base-case outlook for 2031. That is a modeled result within a research framework, not a quoted future market price or a probability-weighted consensus. Investors should read the full assumptions and risk disclosures before comparing the figure with spot trading.

The $1,100 scenario discussed in The Block’s coverage assumes a much larger tokenized-equity market and unusually strong Solana participation. Among the assumptions cited are a 5% tokenization of global stocks and a large share of resulting trading volume flowing through Solana. A scenario built on that scale can help illustrate upside sensitivity, but it also magnifies execution risk. There is no guarantee that securities issuers will tokenize at the modeled pace, or that Solana rather than other blockchains and traditional infrastructure will win most of the business.

For related context, see our earlier report on Solana treasury and staking disclosures.

Even if tokenized assets and payments grow, their relationship to the native token’s value depends on fee structures, network demand, supply dynamics and competition. Low transaction fees can attract activity without making each additional transaction economically equivalent to a large increase in token demand. Layer-two systems, private networks and alternative settlement solutions may also compete for institutional transactions. The mechanism from network activity to investment return needs to be assessed, not assumed. Forecast tables tend to look precise even when the underlying business model is uncertain.

The three cases are most useful as a way to frame questions: how much tokenized volume might actually migrate, how quickly payments grow, what share Solana can secure and how much capacity it would need. The bearish case also reminds readers that technological adoption and investor returns can diverge. Bitwise itself sells crypto investment products, so its commercial perspective should be noted while examining the research. Treat each figure as conditional on the inputs rather than as investment advice or an independent valuation fact.

Scenario analysis becomes more informative when its inputs are varied, rather than when the highest output is presented as a prediction. An investor could test a slower tokenization rollout, tighter fee competition, different staking rewards or a valuation multiple below the research base case. Small changes in several assumptions can compound over five years. Bitwise's work is useful as a model of how network activity might translate into token economics, but competing networks, policy choices and unforeseen technology changes could make realised outcomes very different.

Forecasts make headlines, but assumptions are where the debate belongs. Tracking tokenized equity usage, payment volumes, transaction economics and competition over the next five years will show whether the underlying thesis is getting stronger or weaker.

Reporting sources: Bitwise research introduction · The Block discussion of the scenarios

#5046. Ripple-Backed Evernorth Takes Massive $505 Million XRP Hit

Ripple-backed XRP treasury company Evernorth Holdings has disclosed a significant decrease in the book value of its crypto asset holdings, with total impairment charges amounting to around $505 million before going public on Nasdaq.

Per an SEC filing on Nov. 13, the 346.3 million XRP tokens that Evernorth Holdings owned had a book value of just $341.9 million as of Sept. 30, 2026.

This is compared to the firm's initial accounting of the crypto assets at roughly $846.6 million, with an average acquisition or contribution price of $2.44 per XRP. This represents a nearly 60% decline in book value.

As per the latest filing, Evernorth recorded around $271 million in XRP impairment charges in the first nine months of 2026. This is in addition to the $233.7 million in impairment charges recorded in 2025.

Interestingly, only $6.9 million of the recent impairment charges occurred in the third quarter.

This also explains why Evernorth's XRP assets had a book value so far below their market value at the end of September.

Evernorth calculates impairments based on the lowest observable intraday price of XRP for each batch of tokens acquired. Once the assets are written down, the company is unable to reverse the previous losses if the price rises.

For reference, on Sept. 30, XRP closed the day trading at around $1.49 on Coinbase. At that price, Evernorth's 346.3 million XRP tokens would have been worth roughly $516 million, much higher than the disclosed book value of $341.9 million.

The recent disclosure comes around a month after Evernorth completed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on Oct. 9. It started trading on Nasdaq under the symbol XRPN on Oct. 12.

Following the business combination, Evernorth held around 473 million XRP tokens and had also raised gross cash proceeds of around $300 million.

Its investors include Ripple, SBI Group, Arrington Capital, Pantera Capital, Kraken and GSR.

On Oct. 14, Evernorth announced collaborations with Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo to implement institutional investment strategies starting in Q4 2026.

Meanwhile, its latest SEC filing did not include details on the amount of XRP deployed to generate yield or the returns generated from it.

#5045. Strategy Adds 485 Bitcoin as It Repurchases $228 Million of STRC Preferred Shares

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Strategy has added 485 Bitcoin to its already enormous treasury, but its November 16 disclosure carries another figure that deserves equal attention: the company also repurchased about $228 million of STRC preferred shares. The update is a reminder that digital-asset treasury companies make capital-allocation decisions across both their crypto holdings and the securities used to finance them. Counting BTC alone cannot tell investors whether each step improves their economic position.

Strategy says it bought 485 BTC between November 9 and November 15 for approximately $33.4 million, at an average acquisition price of about $68,887 per coin. The purchase raised aggregate holdings to 850,849 BTC. The company reported an aggregate acquisition cost of around $64.2 billion, equivalent to roughly $75,452 for each Bitcoin held across its history. Those cost figures are not the current market value of the treasury, and the average changes when additional purchases are made. The purchase window also matters because it spans a period of falling Bitcoin prices rather than a single quoted trade.

STRC is part of Strategy’s preferred-capital structure. The company has used such instruments alongside equity and other financing tools to build and manage its balance sheet. Buying back preferred shares below their stated amount can affect obligations, market confidence and the securities still outstanding. It also uses capital that could otherwise serve different purposes. Investors therefore need to compare the BTC acquisition with the repurchase, cash reserves and dividend commitments. Describing the update as an unqualified large Bitcoin bet overlooks the simultaneous management of financing instruments.

For related context, see our earlier report on Twenty One Capital's bitcoin treasury results.

Strategy’s treasury size is a headline measure of exposure, but a common shareholder owns an interest in a company with other securities and obligations ahead of ordinary equity. Increases in BTC can coexist with changes in share count, leverage, dividend requirements and the value of preferred securities. Simple “Bitcoin per company” comparisons do not measure everything shareholders receive. The company provides additional proprietary metrics intended to describe its strategy, but it warns that these are not identical to profitability or conventional balance-sheet valuations.

Bitcoin’s November decline puts the resilience of capital structures under greater scrutiny. A company can keep buying assets while still facing pressure if its shares, preferred securities or access to funding weaken. The key disclosures to monitor are future BTC purchases, security repurchases, cash and liquid reserves, and any changes in capital-raising conditions. The latest acquisition is independently meaningful, but its significance for investors depends on the full balance sheet and the prices at which capital is issued and retired.

Capital structure deserves particular attention because Strategy finances parts of its Bitcoin accumulation through instruments with distinct investor claims. Preferred shares, common equity and debt can behave differently during sharp BTC drawdowns, especially when market prices diverge from accounting values. The relevant questions are not just how many coins were bought but what resources funded the transaction, which obligations were reduced and what exposure remained per common share. Investors should consult the full financing disclosures rather than treating a gross BTC increase as automatic shareholder accretion.

For related context, see our earlier report on JPMorgan's Strategy shareholdings disclosure.

The company has clearly continued acquiring Bitcoin through weakness. The more complete story is that its treasury strategy also includes active management of preferred claims, making both sides of the November 16 announcement essential to understanding the business.

Reporting sources: Strategy November 16 investor release · The Block figures and context

BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF ended an 11-session outflow streak totaling $2.35 billion on Monday, even as the broader market remained underwater for 2026.

The iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) attracted $76.5 million on Nov. 16, recording its first positive session since Oct. 29, according to Farside Investors.

The inflow helped US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds post a combined $7.9 million gain, ending seven consecutive trading sessions of withdrawals totaling approximately $1.91 billion.

However, BlackRock accounted for the entire recovery. Seven competing funds collectively lost $68.6 million, while four recorded no net flows.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs reported combined net inflows of $7.9 million. Positive values indicate net inflows and negative values indicate net outflows. Four funds reported $0.0 million.

Source: Farside Investors, Bitcoin ETF flow table, Nov. 16, 2026

The contrasting performance comes as Bitcoin struggles to recover from its latest selloff, trading around $64,871 as of press time after briefly approaching $61,000 over the weekend.

#5041. Here’s how Ledger’s website was hit by the Optimizely malware attack

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On the 16th of November, Ledger’s public website was infected with malware designed to swap crypto addresses and steal card details. Security researcher Scott Helme traced the code to Optimizely, a website testing provider. His team found compromised scripts tied to 178 organizations, including Ledger, the BBC, and Zoom.

In practice, the malware could swap a copied crypto address for one belonging to the attacker. So if a visitor pasted that address and approved the payment, their crypto could go to the attacker instead.

So far, researchers have traced the malware to Ledger’s public website. Whether it also affected Ledger’s hardware wallets or the Ledger Wallet app remains unclear.

Just over a month earlier, though, Ledger had faced a separate attack involving physical devices. In that case, Ledger confirmed that some wallets sold through a reseller contained unauthorized hardware.

At the time, AMBCrypto reported that the October theft had reached $91 million across more than 470 crypto addresses.

Report URI recorded the cleanup of Ledger’s script at 20:41 UTC that day. Early on the 17th of November, Optimizely said,

We’ve fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects.

Report URI traced about $7,040 in crypto to addresses linked to the attack on the 16th of November. When Galaxy Digital’s Alex Thorn looked at where the money came from, he estimated that victims sent about $2,300. He said,

Most of the rest was the attacker’s own money. The attacker appears to have been very sloppy with their onchain hygiene

However, the number of Ledger visitors who lost funds remains unclear.

A similar breach had hit Polymarket a few weeks earlier. In that case, the malicious code could act on behalf of traders who were already signed in.

On the 29th of October, it sold some traders’ positions and moved funds out of their wallets.

Polymarket paused international trading to stop further losses. It later announced $3.9 million in reimbursements, including about $1.2 million for losses during the pause. By the 30th of October, the company said it had fully refunded 689 of the 726 affected wallets.

#5040. Google uncovers AI hacking tool that turns security fixes into cyberattacks

Researchers discovered an attacker-controlled system capable of identifying software vulnerabilities, generating exploits and executing attacks automatically.

Google has uncovered an AI-powered hacking system capable of transforming software security fixes into automated attacks against vulnerable websites.

In a Nov. 16 report, Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant revealed that attackers were using AI frameworks to identify vulnerabilities, generate malicious code, and execute exploits with minimal human involvement.

The researchers discovered one such system, dubbed exploit_agent, on an exposed staging server containing multiple AI models connected to cybersecurity research and exploitation tools.

The framework was configured to monitor software updates, compare patched code with older versions, and identify weaknesses that developers had recently repaired. It could subsequently generate attack code and execute it automatically, allowing attackers to target websites that had not yet installed the relevant security updates.

This approach exploits the information developers publish when addressing software vulnerabilities. Changes made to repair a flaw can inadvertently reveal how the underlying weakness could be exploited.

Google said the technique lets attackers focus on known vulnerabilities rather than spend time discovering previously unknown security flaws.

The company's investigation also uncovered stolen victim data and malicious scripts capable of conducting internal network reconnaissance, brute-force attacks and installing webshells that provide remote access to compromised servers.

Some tools could remove webshells left by competing attackers, potentially helping the operator retain control over compromised systems.

Google found evidence that the operator was particularly interested in French websites associated with media, entertainment, and education. One recovered example showed the framework examining access-control protections in Spectra, a WordPress plugin used for website development.

Google describes exploit_agent comparing patched code, identifying potential weaknesses, drafting exploits and executing them automatically.

A published fix can guide attack development while website owners are still deploying the update.

The diagram shows Google's configured pipeline, not measured timing, a success rate or proof of an entirely autonomous campaign.

Conceptual process diagram of Google's configured exploit_agent pipeline. Arrows encode sequence and input flow, not elapsed time, conversion rate or successful compromise.

The diagram shows Google's configured pipeline, not measured timing, a success rate or proof of an entirely autonomous campaign.

The discovery marked the first time Google had identified attackers using AI frameworks to fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without human intervention throughout the process.

Google's report also revealed a separate campaign in which suspected North Korean hackers exploited AI-powered development tools to infiltrate cryptocurrency organizations in North America and Europe.

The attackers, tracked as MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE, combined AI-generated identities with fraudulent recruitment campaigns to gain access to corporate systems.

They created fake recruiter profiles on professional networking platforms using AI-generated photographs, then directed prospective victims to fraudulent meeting websites.

Those websites instructed victims to run supposed troubleshooting commands that instead executed malicious scripts.

Once inside an organization, the attackers accessed internal code repositories and modified configuration files used by Anthropic's Claude Code development assistant.

The altered files were designed to automatically download a backdoor known as SOMBERMEME whenever employees launched Claude Code.

Google also discovered that the attackers disguised GitHub access tokens using names associated with Microsoft Copilot, concealing their movements within compromised development environments.

The campaign expanded on North Korea's established use of AI to generate fake resumes, prepare for job interviews, and impersonate Western technology workers seeking remote employment.

Google said the latest intrusions showed how attackers exploited AI development tools already embedded in corporate workflows to distribute malicious software.

Meanwhile, the emergence of autonomous exploitation frameworks threatens to accelerate attacks against organizations running outdated software.

Google warned that automating vulnerability analysis and exploit execution could substantially reduce the time between disclosing a security flaw and exploiting it, leaving website operators with increasingly narrow windows to install protective updates.

#5039. Bitcoin's $90,000 Comeback Now Unlikely, Novogratz Warns

Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz said that the odds of Bitcoin hitting $90,000 by the end of 2026 are slim in light of prevailing macroeconomic headwinds and the growing likelihood that the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates.

During a live event with Anthony Scaramucci at the Digital Assets Forum in New York City, Novogratz was asked if Bitcoin could get back to $90,000 by the end of this year.

"Less likely than it was. You need something to happen," Novogratz said.

His gloomy outlook comes as Bitcoin has struggled to rebound after a devastating drop that saw its price dip as low as $62,000 over the weekend. Bitcoin's price stood at around $64,600 on Nov. 17. The largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization has declined for six consecutive weeks.

A shift in the U.S. monetary policy outlook, namely the prospect of more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve, has been largely to blame for Bitcoin's decline, according to Novogratz.

"At the start of the year, everybody thought the Fed was going to be cutting now," he said.

But high inflation and ongoing supply shocks have forced investors to readjust their expectations.

"Inflation's going up. We've got inflation going up," Novogratz said, warning that inflationary pressures could become increasingly entrenched.

"The Fed's going to hike. At least two more, probably three more," he said.

Novogratz predicted that the Fed would raise rates by 25 basis points in December and then hike again at its next meeting.

He said that higher rates, at least in the near term, tend to weigh on Bitcoin. But the higher cost of government borrowing could eventually provide support for the cryptocurrency.

"Yeah, later," he said in response to the suggestion that higher borrowing costs could be a tailwind for Bitcoin.

"First, you're gonna hike rates. Oh, sell gold, right? You're going to go to the dollar. It's so ingrained in peoples' heads," he said.

"Carry costs going up," he said. Bitcoin doesn't offer the same yield as interest-bearing dollar assets.

"You don't make any interest on Bitcoin in dollars," he said.

In particular, Novogratz said that the massive rise in Treasury yields has been particularly detrimental to the crypto market.

"Literally 40 basis points in like four days of trading. So that's why crypto's down," he said.

He also said that the massive crypto hack could still be weighing on investors' minds, adding to market jitters.

"I think in the back of their minds is the hack," he said.

#5036. Hoskinson: Cardano Not Done Yet

Charles Hoskinson made sure to clear up misunderstandings about whether he thought the work on Cardano was done.

"I never once said Cardano is finished," Hoskinson said in a Nov. 15 post on X.

The comments came after he talked about the completion of Cardano's original roadmap, which raised some questions about his role in the blockchain's future.

He also called out the CEO of the Cardano Foundation, Frederik Gregaard, for not mentioning the Midnight chain when discussing everything the network has accomplished.

In his latest video, uploaded on Nov. 17, Hoskinson celebrated the fact that Midnight had just brought on board its first UK-based banking partner, Monument Bank.

Monument Bank is the first UK bank to offer interest-bearing tokenized retail deposits on a public blockchain, according to an announcement from the Midnight Foundation.

Up to £250 million in customer deposits will be added to Midnight in the first phase, and each tokenized deposit will be backed 1:1 by sterling cash held at the bank.

Monument Bank customers can now earn a fixed 5.2% annual equivalent rate on deposits for 12 months, all without having to deal with cryptocurrencies directly.

Hoskinson was very excited about the scale of the initiative, comparing the planned amount of deposits with the current decentralized finance ecosystem on Cardano.

"It's five times the TVL of Cardano," he said.

The £250 million is the planned initial size of the banking product, not a verified figure for how much is currently deposited on Midnight.

Hoskinson called this one of the most important milestones in his career.

"This is just one of the many things to come, but I think it's one of the most significant things of at least my career," he said.

He added that the team behind Midnight had moved the originally scheduled hard fork from December to November to accommodate the technical needs of Monument Bank.

Despite the milestone, Hoskinson emphasized that it's only the first step in a much larger mission: bringing traditional financial assets onto Midnight.

Hoskinson thinks the main barrier to cryptocurrency adoption is the lack of trust among consumers. He believes that simplifying the user experience without compromising regulatory requirements will allow billions of people to join the blockchain economy.

Hoskinson also shared that there's a big event coming up for the Midnight Foundation on Dec. 15. Developers will showcase future products and technological advancements scheduled for 2027.

#5035. Bitcoin Lightning developers needed two patches to stop a potentially costly attack

The initial July update blocked one crash method but missed a persistent vulnerability that could leave affected nodes unable to restart.

Bitcoin's Core Lightning software required two security patches to eliminate a vulnerability that could repeatedly crash payment nodes and potentially expose funds held in other channels.

A Nov. 13 security disclosure revealed that an initial repair released in July failed to address a second attack method that could keep affected nodes offline even after they restarted.

The vulnerability, tracked as LNF-2026-0004, affected Core Lightning, one of the software implementations used to operate nodes on Bitcoin's Lightning Network.

Security researcher Nishant Bansal discovered that attackers could exploit how Core Lightning assigned identifiers to payment channels, creating duplicate records that caused the software to crash.

The weakness originated in the network's channel-opening process, where each payment channel receives an identifier derived from the Bitcoin transaction output that funds it. Core Lightning could accept multiple channels referencing the same funding output, producing identical identifiers that conflicted with assumptions in its internal software.

In the first attack, a malicious peer could create duplicate pending channels and crash a victim's node simply by reconnecting. The attack required no Bitcoin transaction fees because the fraudulent channels did not need on-chain funding. Each subsequent reconnection could trigger another crash, allowing attackers to repeatedly interrupt payment processing.

However, researchers identified a more persistent variation involving previously closed channels.

By reusing an identifier associated with a closed channel and subsequently closing another channel with the same identifier, attackers could trigger a software failure that persisted across restarts.

Unlike the initial attack, this method required on-chain transaction fees but could leave the node unable to recover without a software upgrade.

Core Lightning developers addressed the original vulnerability in version 26.06.6, released on July 22, after researchers privately reported the reconnection attack earlier that month.

The update prevented new channels from reusing funding outputs associated with existing live channels. It also modified connection handling to prevent duplicate records already stored from triggering the original crash.

However, the protection did not extend to identifiers associated with closed channels, leaving the second attack route available.

Researcher Crypt-iQ independently identified the remaining weakness, prompting developers to introduce broader safeguards in version 26.06.8, released Sept. 22.

The second update expanded duplicate-identifier checks across active and closed channels belonging to different peers. It also allowed nodes containing previously stored duplicate records to recover without repeatedly crashing.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

July’s repair checked live channels. September’s also covered closed channels and allowed recovery from duplicates already stored.

The first fix blocked outpoints reused among that peer’s live channels and handled reconnect duplicates. Closed-channel collisions could still cause a persistent restart loop.

The broader fix rejected IDs used by live or closed channels across all peers and let nodes load and close duplicates already stored.

Operators should upgrade to the latest release to prevent collisions and handle stored duplicates.

The closed-channel loop shown is the documented persistent path; a separate free nonpersistent path also existed. This qualitative schematic does not show exploitation, losses or affected-node counts.

Qualitative schematic of the common collision mechanism and two historical patch scopes. Toggle compares July 22 v26.06.6 with September 22 v26.06.8. Connectors show software paths, not counts, timing or money flows.

The closed-channel loop shown is the documented persistent path; a separate free nonpersistent path also existed. This qualitative schematic does not show exploitation, losses or affected-node counts.

The potential financial consequences extended beyond disrupted Lightning payments.

According to the advisory, nodes forced offline could lose the ability to monitor Bitcoin's blockchain for attempts to settle channels using revoked transaction states.

That could allow dishonest counterparties to claim funds using outdated channel balances. Offline nodes could also miss deadlines for collecting time-sensitive payments, placing Bitcoin held in unrelated channels at risk.

The researchers did not report confirmed exploitation or financial losses.

The findings affect Core Lightning versions preceding the complete September repair, with the reconnection vulnerability dating back to version 0.12.0 and the persistent closed-channel crash introduced in version 25.05.

Developers have since released additional security updates, including version 26.06.10, which addresses other vulnerabilities involving channel operations, payment resolution, and remote crashes.

Core Lightning's maintainers have urged operators to upgrade to the latest release to protect their nodes against the disclosed weaknesses.

#5034. Bitcoin Policy Institute Renames to Finney Foundation for Open Technology

The Bitcoin Policy Institute announced Tuesday that it is now the Finney Foundation for Open Technology, a new parent organization whose brief spans open-source artificial intelligence, digital cash and encrypted messaging. The institute’s bitcoin work continues inside the foundation, and bitcoin remains a primary focus.

The name honors Hal Finney (1956-2014), a cryptographer and software developer who helped build the email encryption program PGP, ran one of the first anonymous remailers and received the first bitcoin transaction from Satoshi Nakamoto in January 2009. In a November 1992 essay, Finney wrote that the computer “can be used as a tool to liberate and protect people, rather than to control them.” He was diagnosed with ALS the same year he received that first transaction and died in 2014.

Washington is now writing the rules for artificial intelligence, the foundation said, and fear drives much of that debate. As the Bitcoin Policy Institute did for bitcoin, the Finney Foundation said it will argue that open systems outcompete closed ones, that individuals should control the tools they rely on, and that American strength comes from building in the open.

“We set out to make Washington think about Bitcoin differently — to educate them on the importance of open monetary networks,” said David Zell, president of the Finney Foundation. “Our fellows now serve in congressional offices for both parties and in the executive branch. Our ideas have shaped discourse and policy. Our expansion will help us stay at the forefront of today’s most consequential policy debates, especially those around open source AI.”

That argument was already on stage in September at Freedom Tech DC, the institute’s Washington summit, formerly the Bitcoin Policy Summit. The invite-only gathering put open-source and open-weight AI, data centers and energy infrastructure on the agenda alongside bitcoin and dollar-backed stablecoins.

Block co-founder Jack Dorsey said there that “the next and probably largest element [of freedom technology] is open intelligence and making sure that it’s not locked up in the hands of any one government or any one company… that’s where we’re going to get the best outcomes.”

Alongside the new name, the foundation published an Open Technology Declaration, titled “For Us, Not Over Us,” which argues for machines that serve people rather than rule over them. The text takes up Finney’s line about computers as tools of liberation and says the foundation will offer research, policy ideas and educational programs aimed at that goal. It asks who the new machines are for and who is in control of them, and it calls for people to build the tools they need without waiting for permission.

It is also launching an inaugural class of Finney Fellows, researchers with expertise spanning machine intelligence, free speech, national security, biotechnology and space. The foundation says that cohort will be named Wednesday at 10 a.m. ET. A separate roster of Bitcoin Policy Institute fellows remains listed on the same page.

The shift does not retire the institute’s bitcoin brief. The Bitcoin Policy Institute, founded in 2022, has run a congressional fellowship program to place bitcoin specialists in congressional offices, joined the State Department’s Freedom Tech Excellence Program as a founding partner, and urged Congress to include bitcoin in proposed de minimis tax relief. In August, it named Conner Brown executive director as it expanded its leadership team.

The Finney Foundation describes itself as a nonpartisan, nonprofit 501(c)(3) think tank in Washington, D.C. Zell is president. Brown remains executive director on the new staff list. For now, the bitcoin think tank still exists, just under a wider roof, with a new class of fellows due to be named in the morning.

#5031. Bitcoin developer verifies 164 million unspent coins in just 72 seconds

An experimental cryptographic system could dramatically reduce Bitcoin node setup times by replacing extensive historical checks with compact mathematical proofs.

A Bitcoin developer has shown how to verify a 9.39 GB blockchain snapshot in just 72 seconds, potentially making it easier and faster to run Bitcoin nodes.

The developer, identified as l-henri, disclosed the experiment in a Nov. 13 Delving Bitcoin post, describing a system that uses cryptographic proofs to check Bitcoin's existing transaction records without independently processing its entire history.

The experiment involved a snapshot containing approximately 164.5 million unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) at Bitcoin block 972,500. These outputs represent Bitcoin that has been received but not yet spent, forming the database nodes use to determine whether coins remain available for transactions.

Using an arm64 computer with approximately 0.5 GB of memory, the developer checked that the snapshot matched the records established by a cryptographic proof.

The process took approximately 72 seconds, with nearly all that time spent reading the 9.39 GB file. Separately, the developer demonstrated that a compact 1.6 MB proof could be verified in a web browser in about half a second.

The achievement could help address a practical challenge of running Bitcoin infrastructure: the time and computing resources required to verify historical blockchain activity before a node becomes fully operational.

Bitcoin nodes help secure the network by independently checking transactions and enforcing its rules.

Traditionally, setting up a fully validating node involves downloading and processing BTC's historical transactions to reconstruct the current database of spendable coins.

Bitcoin Core already offers a shortcut through a feature called assumeUTXO, which lets nodes start operating using a snapshot of the blockchain's transaction state. However, the software continues verifying historical transactions in the background to confirm that the snapshot accurately reflects Bitcoin's records.

L-henri's experiment proposes replacing that additional verification work with a cryptographic proof. This approach could let new nodes accept a verified snapshot without repeating extensive historical calculations, potentially reducing setup time and resource requirements.

The developer's system uses STARK proofs, which allow computers to verify specified calculations without repeating every step themselves. In this experiment, the proof covered BTC's block headers from its beginning and checked changes to unspent coins between blocks 935,001 and 972,500.

The experiment replays a bounded range from a trusted snapshot. Its two reported timing figures measure different checks.

The author reports a 72-second check of the 9.39 GB snapshot against the proof's commitments.

The author reports checking the 1.6 MB proof in about half a second, separately from the snapshot-file benchmark.

Checking the file against a proof retains the trusted starting snapshot and the omission of scripts and signatures.

Benchmarks are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced here. The replay starts from Core's trusted snapshot at block 935,000, omits scripts and signatures, and has no external review. Neither measurement establishes total node setup time.

Source-bound process diagrams from the project's reported measurements and limitations. The replay path is schematic, not proportional to block count or time. Panel selection compares two different verification jobs; it is not a speedup calculation.

Benchmarks are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced here. The replay starts from Core's trusted snapshot at block 935,000, omits scripts and signatures, and has no external review. Neither measurement establishes total node setup time.

However, the calculations started from an existing trusted Bitcoin Core snapshot at block 935,000 rather than rebuilding the entire transaction history. The system also excluded checks of transaction scripts and signatures, meaning it does not yet provide the same verification guarantees as a fully validating BTC node.

These limitations remain important as the developer considers integrating the technology into Bitcoin Core.

In the November disclosure, l-henri proposed testing a modification that would let Bitcoin Core accept proof-backed snapshots and skip its existing background validation process.

That would mark a departure from Bitcoin Core's current approach, which independently checks historical records even after loading a snapshot.

The project remains experimental and has not undergone an external security review. Bitcoin Core also does not currently support the proposed integration.

The next step is to test whether the proof system can provide sufficient verification guarantees to replace historical checks without weakening the security assumptions BTC nodes rely on.
